/// Opens the package named `name`, associated with the project `project`
/// when given (Phase 7H; persisted since 7H.1).
///
/// The association resolution mirrors the project service: a requested
/// parent must be a valid project name, the recorded association is
/// authoritative on reopen, and a conflicting requested parent is rejected.
/// The resolved association is recorded on the real [`Package`] object and
/// persisted atomically into the `packages/` category. Fails when a package
/// is already open (duplicate-open rejection), a name is invalid, the
/// persisted state is corrupt, or the write fails.
fn open_package(
    state: &RefCell<PackageState>,
    name: &str,
    project: Option<&str>,
) -> crate::Result<()> {
    let mut state = state.borrow_mut();
    if state.package.is_some() {
        return Err(crate::Error::ActiveObject(
            "a package is already open".to_owned(),
        ));
    }
    let id = ActiveObjectId::new(ActiveObjectKind::Package, name)?;
    // The requested parent, when given, must itself be a valid project name.
    if let Some(parent) = project {
        ActiveObjectId::new(ActiveObjectKind::Project, parent)?;
    }
    // Restore the persisted association when present (missing state opens
    // fresh); corrupt or mismatched state is a deterministic rejection.
    let persisted = match load_state_text(&state.pss, &state.syss, PACKAGE_CATEGORY, name)? {
        Some(text) => parse_package_state(&text, name)?,
        None => None,
    };
    // The recorded association is authoritative; a conflicting requested
    // parent is an invalid association and is never silently ignored.
    let association = match (&persisted, project) {
        (Some(recorded), Some(requested)) if recorded != requested => {
            return Err(crate::Error::ActiveObject(format!(
                "package {name:?} is already associated with project {recorded:?}"
            )));
        }
        (Some(recorded), _) => Some(recorded.clone()),
        (None, requested) => requested.map(str::to_owned),
    };
    let mut package = Package::new(id);
    match &association {
        Some(parent) => {
            package.open_in(ActiveObjectId::new(ActiveObjectKind::Project, parent)?)?;
        }
        None => package.open()?,
    }
    // Persist the package state (name + resolved association).
    persist_state(
        &state.pss,
        &state.syss,
        PACKAGE_CATEGORY,
        name,
        &package_state_text(name, association.as_deref()),
    )?;
    state.package = Some(package);
    Ok(())
}

/// Closes the open package (Phase 7H). Fails when no package is open
/// (closing a nonexistent object).
///
/// Closing does **not** delete the persisted state: reopening restores it.
fn close_package(state: &RefCell<PackageState>) -> crate::Result<()> {
    let mut state = state.borrow_mut();
    let mut package = state
        .package
        .take()
        .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error::ActiveObject("no package is open".to_owned()))?;
    package.close()
}

/// The severity of a structured log record (Phase 7H.2).
///
/// The smallest deterministic severity vocabulary the platform log needs;
/// no external logging dependency.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) enum LogSeverity {
    /// Informational record.
    Info,
    /// A warning worth surfacing.
    Warning,
    /// An error.
    Error,
}

impl LogSeverity {
    /// The stable name of this severity ("Info", "Warning", "Error").
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            LogSeverity::Info => "Info",
            LogSeverity::Warning => "Warning",
            LogSeverity::Error => "Error",
        }
    }

    /// Parses a severity from its stable name.
    fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<LogSeverity> {
        match name {
            "Info" => Some(LogSeverity::Info),
            "Warning" => Some(LogSeverity::Warning),
            "Error" => Some(LogSeverity::Error),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// A structured log record (Phase 7H.2): a deterministic sequence number
/// (1-based within the session), a severity, the source/domain and the
/// message. The sequence is derived from the record order, so it is stable
/// and deterministic.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct LogRecord {
    sequence: u64,
    severity: LogSeverity,
    source: String,
    message: String,
}

impl LogRecord {
    /// Creates a record with the given `sequence`.
    fn new(sequence: u64, severity: LogSeverity, source: &str, message: &str) -> LogRecord {
        LogRecord {
            sequence,
            severity,
            source: source.to_owned(),
            message: message.to_owned(),
        }
    }

    /// The deterministic sequence number of this record (1-based).
    ///
    /// The lib build reads records through the summary and the persistence
    /// lines; the typed accessors are verified by the module tests and
    /// consumed by future phases that render or filter the log.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn sequence(&self) -> u64 {
        self.sequence
    }

    /// The severity of this record.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn severity(&self) -> LogSeverity {
        self.severity
    }

    /// The source/domain that produced this record.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn source(&self) -> &str {
        &self.source
    }

    /// The record message.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn message(&self) -> &str {
        &self.message
    }
}

/// The settings state of the settings domain (Phase 7H.2): a controlled
/// key/value map with deterministic defaults, validated values, and
/// per-key persistence through the existing stack (each key is one file in
/// the `settings/` category, written atomically).
///
/// Theme and view are settings-backed platform state: the `theme` key is
/// validated against the supported themes and defaults to `light`; the
/// `view` key defaults to `editor`. No rendering, no UI — the Frontend
/// consumes this state later.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct SettingsState {
    /// The storage space over the platform storage root.
    syss: Syss,
    /// The serialization service (the `.ra` text codec).
    pss: Pss,
    /// The controlled settings (persisted keys only; defaults are derived,
    /// never written).
    values: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Whether the persisted settings have been loaded. Loading is lazy so
    /// corrupt persisted state never fails the boot — it fails the first
    /// settings operation deterministically.
    loaded: bool,
}

impl SettingsState {
    /// Creates the settings state over the given storage root.
    fn with_root(root: PathBuf) -> SettingsState {
        SettingsState {
            syss: Syss::new(root),
            pss: Pss::new(),
            values: BTreeMap::new(),
            loaded: false,
        }
    }

    /// The deterministic default of a known setting, if any.
    fn default_for(key: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
        match key {
            "theme" => Some("light"),
            "view" => Some("editor"),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The supported values of a known setting, if the setting is validated
    /// against a fixed set.
    fn supported_values(key: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]> {
        match key {
            "theme" => Some(&["light", "dark"]),
            "view" => Some(&["editor", "terminal", "ide"]),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Validates a setting update: the key must be a valid storage name, the
    /// value must be non-empty and free of line breaks/NUL (it is persisted
    /// as file content), and a setting with a fixed value set only accepts a
    /// supported value.
    fn validate(key: &str, value: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        crate::syss::validate_name(key)?;
        if value.is_empty() {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(
                "setting value is empty".to_owned(),
            ));
        }
        if value.contains(['\n', '\0']) {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(format!(
                "setting value {value:?} contains a line break or NUL"
            )));
        }
        if let Some(supported) = Self::supported_values(key) {
            if !supported.contains(&value) {
                return Err(crate::Error::ActiveObject(format!(
                    "unsupported value {value:?} for setting {key:?}"
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Loads the persisted settings from the `settings/` category (lazy,
    /// once). A corrupt entry fails deterministically.
    fn load(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        if self.loaded {
            return Ok(());
        }
        for name in self.syss.list(SETTINGS_CATEGORY)? {
            if let Some(value) = load_state_text(&self.pss, &self.syss, SETTINGS_CATEGORY, &name)? {
                self.values.insert(name, value);
            }
        }
        self.loaded = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Validates and updates the setting `key` to `value`, persisting it
    /// atomically into the `settings/` category.
    fn set(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.load()?;
        Self::validate(key, value)?;
        persist_state(&self.pss, &self.syss, SETTINGS_CATEGORY, key, value)?;
        self.values.insert(key.to_owned(), value.to_owned());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Retrieves the setting `key`: the persisted value, or the
    /// deterministic default for a known setting. Unknown keys have no
    /// value.
    fn get(&mut self, key: &str) -> crate::Result<Option<String>> {
        self.load()?;
        if let Some(value) = self.values.get(key) {
            return Ok(Some(value.clone()));
        }
        Ok(Self::default_for(key).map(str::to_owned))
    }

    /// The deterministic inspection summary of this state (sorted keys,
    /// persisted values only).
    fn summary(&mut self) -> crate::Result<String> {
        self.load()?;
        Ok(if self.values.is_empty() {
            "settings: (empty)".to_owned()
        } else {
            let entries = self
                .values
                .iter()
                .map(|(key, value)| format!("{key}={value}"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ");
            format!("settings: {entries}")
        })
    }
}

/// The deterministic behavior of the settings service (Phase 7H.2):
/// `Set { key, value }` validates and persists a setting, `Get(key)`
/// retrieves it (value or default), and a `Request` carrying `Inspect`
/// answers with the state summary.
fn invoke_settings(
    invocation: &ServiceInvocation,
    state: &RefCell<SettingsState>,
) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
    use BackboneMessageKind as Kind;
    match (invocation.kind(), invocation.operation()) {
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Accept) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Set { key, value }) => {
            Ok(active_object_outcome(state.borrow_mut().set(&key, &value)))
        }
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Get(key)) => match state.borrow_mut().get(&key) {
            Ok(Some(value)) => Ok(ServiceResult::Inspected(value)),
            _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
        },
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Inspect) => {
            Ok(active_object_inspection(state.borrow_mut().summary()))
        }
        (Kind::Notification, _) => Ok(ServiceResult::Accepted),
        _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
    }
}

/// The history state of the history domain (Phase 7H.2): an ordered list of
/// recorded platform operations, persisted as one line per entry in the
/// `history/history` file through the existing stack.
///
/// Application/platform history only — **not** RA runtime/execution
/// history. The service never inspects another service's state; the caller
/// provides the entry text explicitly.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct HistoryState {
    /// The storage space over the platform storage root.
    syss: Syss,
    /// The serialization service (the `.ra` text codec).
    pss: Pss,
    /// The recorded entries, in record order.
    entries: Vec<String>,
    /// Whether the persisted history has been loaded (lazy, once).
    loaded: bool,
}

impl HistoryState {
    /// Creates the history state over the given storage root.
    fn with_root(root: PathBuf) -> HistoryState {
        HistoryState {
            syss: Syss::new(root),
            pss: Pss::new(),
            entries: Vec::new(),
            loaded: false,
        }
    }

    /// Loads the persisted history (lazy, once). Corrupt state fails
    /// deterministically.
    fn load(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        if self.loaded {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(text) = load_state_text(&self.pss, &self.syss, HISTORY_CATEGORY, HISTORY_FILE)?
        {
            self.entries = text.lines().map(str::to_owned).collect();
        }
        self.loaded = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Validates a history entry: non-empty and free of line breaks/NUL (it
    /// is persisted as one line).
    fn validate(entry: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        if entry.is_empty() {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(
                "history entry is empty".to_owned(),
            ));
        }
        if entry.contains(['\n', '\0']) {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(format!(
                "history entry {entry:?} contains a line break or NUL"
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Records `entry` at the end of the history and persists it.
    fn record(&mut self, entry: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.load()?;
        Self::validate(entry)?;
        self.entries.push(entry.to_owned());
        self.persist()
    }

    /// Clears the history, including its persisted state.
    fn clear(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.load()?;
        self.entries.clear();
        self.delete_persisted()
    }

    /// Writes the whole history into the `history/history` file atomically.
    fn persist(&self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        persist_state(
            &self.pss,
            &self.syss,
            HISTORY_CATEGORY,
            HISTORY_FILE,
            &self.entries.join("\n"),
        )
    }

    /// Deletes the persisted history file (a missing file is fine).
    fn delete_persisted(&self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        match self.syss.delete(HISTORY_CATEGORY, HISTORY_FILE) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(crate::Error::NotFound { .. }) => Ok(()),
            Err(err) => Err(err),
        }
    }

    /// The deterministic inspection summary of this state.
    fn summary(&mut self) -> crate::Result<String> {
        self.load()?;
        Ok(if self.entries.is_empty() {
            "history: 0 entries".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!(
                "history: {} entries [{}]",
                self.entries.len(),
                self.entries.join(", ")
            )
        })
    }
}

/// The deterministic behavior of the history service (Phase 7H.2).
fn invoke_history(
    invocation: &ServiceInvocation,
    state: &RefCell<HistoryState>,
) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
    use BackboneMessageKind as Kind;
    match (invocation.kind(), invocation.operation()) {
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Accept) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Record(entry)) => {
            Ok(active_object_outcome(state.borrow_mut().record(&entry)))
        }
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Clear) => {
            Ok(active_object_outcome(state.borrow_mut().clear()))
        }
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Inspect) => {
            Ok(active_object_inspection(state.borrow_mut().summary()))
        }
        (Kind::Notification, _) => Ok(ServiceResult::Accepted),
        _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
    }
}

/// The log state of the log domain (Phase 7H.2): the smallest real platform
/// logging subsystem — an ordered list of structured [`LogRecord`]s
/// (severity, source/domain, message, deterministic sequence), persisted as
/// one `<severity> <source> <message>` line per record in the `logs/log`
/// file through the existing stack.
///
/// The log is a SySS/application concern — **not** an RA language/runtime
/// logger. The Phase 7F.1 proof behavior (a bare command completes, a
/// notification completes) is preserved.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct LogState {
    /// The storage space over the platform storage root.
    syss: Syss,
    /// The serialization service (the `.ra` text codec).
    pss: Pss,
    /// The structured records, in record order (sequence = 1-based index).
    records: Vec<LogRecord>,
    /// Whether the persisted log has been loaded (lazy, once).
    loaded: bool,
}

impl LogState {
    /// Creates the log state over the given storage root.
    fn with_root(root: PathBuf) -> LogState {
        LogState {
            syss: Syss::new(root),
            pss: Pss::new(),
            records: Vec::new(),
            loaded: false,
        }
    }

    /// Loads the persisted log (lazy, once). A line that cannot be parsed
    /// back into a record is corrupt state and fails deterministically.
    fn load(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        if self.loaded {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(text) = load_state_text(&self.pss, &self.syss, LOG_CATEGORY, LOG_FILE)? {
            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
                let record =
                    Self::parse_line(line).ok_or_else(|| corrupt_state("log", LOG_FILE))?;
                self.records.push(LogRecord::new(
                    index as u64 + 1,
                    record.0,
                    &record.1,
                    &record.2,
                ));
            }
        }
        self.loaded = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Parses one persisted line back into `(severity, source, message)`.
    fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Option<(LogSeverity, String, String)> {
        let mut parts = line.splitn(3, ' ');
        let severity = LogSeverity::from_name(parts.next()?)?;
        let source = parts.next()?;
        let message = parts.next()?;
        Some((severity, source.to_owned(), message.to_owned()))
    }

    /// Validates a structured record: the source must be non-empty and free
    /// of whitespace/line breaks/NUL (it is persisted as one token), and the
    /// message must be non-empty and free of line breaks/NUL (one line).
    fn validate(source: &str, message: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        if source.is_empty() || source.contains([' ', '\t', '\n', '\0']) {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(format!(
                "log source {source:?} is invalid"
            )));
        }
        if message.is_empty() {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName("log message is empty".to_owned()));
        }
        if message.contains(['\n', '\0']) {
            return Err(crate::Error::InvalidName(format!(
                "log message {message:?} contains a line break or NUL"
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Records a structured record at the end of the log and persists it.
    fn record(&mut self, severity: LogSeverity, source: &str, message: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.load()?;
        Self::validate(source, message)?;
        self.records.push(LogRecord::new(
            self.records.len() as u64 + 1,
            severity,
            source,
            message,
        ));
        self.persist()
    }

    /// The back-compatible message path: `Record(message)` records an
    /// `Info` record sourced from the log domain itself.
    fn record_message(&mut self, message: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.record(LogSeverity::Info, "log", message)
    }

    /// Clears the log, including its persisted state.
    fn clear(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        self.load()?;
        self.records.clear();
        match self.syss.delete(LOG_CATEGORY, LOG_FILE) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(crate::Error::NotFound { .. }) => Ok(()),
            Err(err) => Err(err),
        }
    }

    /// Writes the whole log into the `logs/log` file atomically.
    fn persist(&self) -> crate::Result<()> {
        let text = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .map(|record| {
                format!(
                    "{} {} {}",
                    record.severity.name(),
                    record.source,
                    record.message
                )
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n");
        persist_state(&self.pss, &self.syss, LOG_CATEGORY, LOG_FILE, &text)
    }

    /// The deterministic inspection summary of this state, listing the
    /// record messages (the structure is exposed through the records and the
    /// persisted lines).
    fn summary(&mut self) -> crate::Result<String> {
        self.load()?;
        let messages = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .map(|record| record.message.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        Ok(if messages.is_empty() {
            "log: 0 entries".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!("log: {} entries [{}]", messages.len(), messages.join(", "))
        })
    }
}

/// The deterministic behavior of the log service (Phase 7H.2).
fn invoke_log(
    invocation: &ServiceInvocation,
    state: &RefCell<LogState>,
) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
    use BackboneMessageKind as Kind;
    match (invocation.kind(), invocation.operation()) {
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Accept) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Record(message)) => Ok(active_object_outcome(
            state.borrow_mut().record_message(&message),
        )),
        (
            Kind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                severity,
                source,
                message,
            },
        ) => Ok(active_object_outcome(
            state.borrow_mut().record(severity, &source, &message),
        )),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Clear) => {
            Ok(active_object_outcome(state.borrow_mut().clear()))
        }
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Inspect) => {
            Ok(active_object_inspection(state.borrow_mut().summary()))
        }
        (Kind::Notification, _) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
    }
}

/// Maps a fallible inspection to the service outcome (Phase 7H.2): the
/// summary when the state loads, a deterministic rejection otherwise.
fn active_object_inspection(result: crate::Result<String>) -> ServiceResult {
    match result {
        Ok(summary) => ServiceResult::Inspected(summary),
        Err(_) => ServiceResult::Rejected,
    }
}

/// The platform capability state of the device domain: a fixed,
/// deterministic capability description. No hardware, device or persistence
/// behavior lives here.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct ProbeState {
    capability: String,
}

impl ProbeState {
    /// Creates the capability state from a fixed description.
    fn new(capability: &str) -> ProbeState {
        ProbeState {
            capability: capability.to_owned(),
        }
    }

    /// The deterministic inspection summary of this state, prefixed by
    /// `label` ("device").
    fn summary(&self, label: &str) -> String {
        format!("{label}: {}", self.capability)
    }
}

/// A storage-stack service of the platform's storage architecture (Phase
/// 7G).
///
/// The platform's storage is provided by three `ra-syss` services built on
/// the `ra-persistence` codec layer. FSS is **not** a separate component in
/// the implementation: the System Storage Space ([`crate::Syss`]) is the
/// file/storage-system boundary of the architecture (atomic writes, storage
/// categories, device files), PSS is the Program Serialization Service
/// ([`crate::Pss`], the artifact codec boundary) and Recovery is the
/// crash-recovery service ([`crate::Recovery`]). The Storage Service
/// **represents** this stack; it does not implement it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum StorageStackService {
    /// The System Storage Space ([`crate::Syss`]): owns the storage root,
    /// the categories, the device files and the atomic writes.
    Syss,
    /// The Program Serialization Service ([`crate::Pss`]): artifact bytes
    /// through the codec layer over `ra-persistence`.
    Pss,
    /// Crash recovery ([`crate::Recovery`]): resolves interrupted atomic
    /// writes.
    Recovery,
}

impl StorageStackService {
    /// The storage stack, in stable order.
    const ALL: [StorageStackService; 3] = [
        StorageStackService::Syss,
        StorageStackService::Pss,
        StorageStackService::Recovery,
    ];

    /// The stable name of this storage-stack service ("syss", "pss",
    /// "recovery").
    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            StorageStackService::Syss => "syss",
            StorageStackService::Pss => "pss",
            StorageStackService::Recovery => "recovery",
        }
    }
}

/// The real storage-domain state of the Storage Service (Phase 7G.1).
///
/// The live storage boundary behind the platform:
///
/// `StorageService → Syss (storage space) · Pss (serialization) · Recovery
/// (crash recovery) → ra-persistence (codec layer) → persistent storage`
///
/// The state holds the **real storage stack** — the [`Syss`] handle over
/// the platform storage root, the fully wired [`Pss`] codec registry and
/// the [`Recovery`] crash-recovery service — and performs the real storage
/// operations (Save / Load / Recover) through those existing services. It
/// implements no persistence: the `ra-persistence` codec architecture, PSS
/// and Recovery are untouched, and the service only *calls* them.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct StorageState {
    syss: Syss,
    pss: Pss,
    recovery: Recovery,
}

impl StorageState {
    /// Creates the storage-domain state over the given platform storage
    /// root.
    fn new(root: PathBuf) -> StorageState {
        StorageState {
            syss: Syss::new(root),
            pss: Pss::new(),
            recovery: Recovery::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Returns the platform storage root this state is wired to.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests verify the wired root
    /// (TODO(Phase7G.1)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    fn root(&self) -> &Path {
        self.syss.root()
    }

    /// The deterministic inspection summary of this state: the storage
    /// stack and the number of storage categories.
    fn summary(&self) -> String {
        let stack = StorageStackService::ALL
            .iter()
            .map(|service| service.name())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(",");
        format!(
            "storage: stack={stack}; categories={}",
            StorageCategory::ALL.len()
        )
    }

    /// Saves `artifact` into the storage space through the existing stack:
    /// the artifact is validated and serialized by PSS, and the produced
    /// bytes are stored by Syss under `category`/`name` (atomic write).
    fn save(
        &self,
        category: StorageCategory,
        name: &str,
        artifact: &Artifact,
    ) -> crate::Result<()> {
        let format = artifact_format(artifact);
        self.pss.validate(format, artifact)?;
        let bytes = self.pss.serialize(format, artifact)?;
        self.syss.save(category, name, &bytes)
    }

    /// Loads the named storage entry through the existing stack: Syss reads
    /// the bytes, and PSS deserializes them with the codec of the name's
    /// format extension.
    fn load(&self, category: StorageCategory, name: &str) -> crate::Result<Artifact> {
        let bytes = self.syss.load(category, name)?;
        let format = format_from_name(name)?;
        self.pss.deserialize(format, &bytes)
    }

    /// Runs crash recovery over the platform storage root through the
    /// existing [`Recovery`] service.
    fn recover(&self) -> crate::Result<RecoveryReport> {
        self.recovery.recover(self.syss.root())
    }
}

/// The format codec key of an artifact, derived from its kind.
///
/// Programs use their canonical format (`.ra`/`.rab`); snapshots are `.raf`
/// and packages `.rap` — the frozen codec mapping.
fn artifact_format(artifact: &Artifact) -> ra_persistence::Format {
    match artifact {
        Artifact::Program(program) => program.format(),
        Artifact::Snapshot(_) => ra_persistence::Format::Raf,
        Artifact::Package(_) => ra_persistence::Format::Rap,
    }
}

/// Resolves the format codec key from a storage name's extension.
///
/// A name without a supported format extension cannot be loaded — there is
/// no codec to deserialize it with.
fn format_from_name(name: &str) -> crate::Result<ra_persistence::Format> {
    let extension = name.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or(name);
    ra_persistence::Format::from_extension(extension).ok_or_else(|| {
        crate::Error::InvalidName(format!("{name:?} has no supported format extension"))
    })
}

/// The deterministic representation of a loaded artifact (Phase 7G.1).
fn loaded_summary(name: &str, artifact: &Artifact) -> String {
    let representation = match artifact {
        Artifact::Program(program) => format!("program: {}", program.text()),
        Artifact::Snapshot(snapshot) => format!("snapshot: {}", snapshot.source()),
        Artifact::Package(package) => format!("package: {} entries", package.len()),
    };
    format!("loaded {name}: {representation}")
}

/// The deterministic summary of a recovery report (Phase 7G.1).
fn recovery_summary(report: &RecoveryReport) -> String {
    format!(
        "recovery: scanned={}, restored={}, removed={}, failed={}",
        report.scanned,
        report.restored.len(),
        report.removed.len(),
        report.failed.len()
    )
}

/// The shared deterministic behavior of the probe services (storage,
/// device): the capability probe completes, and the inspection answers with
/// `summary` (the capability description, provided by the service's domain
/// state).
fn invoke_probe(
    invocation: &ServiceInvocation,
    summary: impl Fn() -> String,
) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
    use BackboneMessageKind as Kind;
    match (invocation.kind(), invocation.operation()) {
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Accept) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Probe) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Inspect) => Ok(ServiceResult::Inspected(summary())),
        (Kind::Notification, _) => Ok(ServiceResult::Accepted),
        _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
    }
}

/// The deterministic behavior of the storage service (Phase 7G.1).
///
/// The storage service is the platform's **request/response storage
/// service**: its real operations — `Save`, `Load`, `Recover` — travel as
/// Requests and are answered with the typed [`ServiceResult`] of the
/// operation (`Completed`, `Loaded`, `Recovered`), or `Rejected` when the
/// operation cannot be performed (a deterministic service failure — the
/// underlying `ra-syss` storage error stays at the Syss/Pss/Recovery layer;
/// transport success never means storage success). The proof operations
/// (`Accept`, `Probe`) and the inspection (`Inspect`) are preserved.
fn invoke_storage(
    invocation: &ServiceInvocation,
    state: &RefCell<StorageState>,
) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
    use BackboneMessageKind as Kind;
    match (invocation.kind(), invocation.operation()) {
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Accept) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Command, ServiceOperation::Probe) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Inspect) => {
            Ok(ServiceResult::Inspected(state.borrow().summary()))
        }
        (
            Kind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::Save {
                category,
                name,
                artifact,
            },
        ) => match state.borrow().save(category, &name, &artifact) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(ServiceResult::Completed),
            Err(_) => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
        },
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Load { category, name }) => {
            match state.borrow().load(category, &name) {
                Ok(artifact) => Ok(ServiceResult::Loaded(loaded_summary(&name, &artifact))),
                Err(_) => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
            }
        }
        (Kind::Request, ServiceOperation::Recover) => match state.borrow().recover() {
            Ok(report) => Ok(ServiceResult::Recovered(recovery_summary(&report))),
            Err(_) => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
        },
        (Kind::Notification, _) => Ok(ServiceResult::Accepted),
        _ => Ok(ServiceResult::Rejected),
    }
}

/// The Workspace Service — owns the workspace domain state (Phase 7H).
///
/// Domain state: the real [`Workspace`] active object and — because the
/// existing hub set has no Document hub — the real [`Document`] active
/// object of the workspace domain, persisted through the existing Syss/PSS
/// stack (the `files` category). Operations: `Open(name)` opens the
/// workspace, `Close` closes it, `Inspect` answers with the workspace
/// summary; the document operations (`OpenDocument`, `CloseDocument`,
/// `SaveDocument`, `SaveDocumentAs`, `ImportDocument`, `ExportDocument`,
/// `InspectDocument`, `SetDocumentContent`) manage the active document. No
/// project discovery, package loading, IDE behavior or filesystem scanning
/// (future phases).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct WorkspaceService {
    core: ServiceCore,
    state: RefCell<WorkspaceState>,
}

impl WorkspaceService {
    /// Creates the Workspace Service, owned by the Workspace Authority, over
    /// the platform default storage root (Phase 7H).
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`WorkspaceService::with_root`] with the resolved platform root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> WorkspaceService {
        Self::with_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the Workspace Service over the given storage root (Phase 7H,
    /// additive).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// workspace boundary through this constructor; the tests use it for
    /// isolation.
    pub(crate) fn with_root(root: PathBuf) -> WorkspaceService {
        WorkspaceService {
            core: ServiceCore::new(ServiceId::new("workspace"), HubId::WORKSPACE),
            state: RefCell::new(WorkspaceState::new(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl Service for WorkspaceService {
    fn core(&self) -> &ServiceCore {
        &self.core
    }

    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
        invoke_workspace(invocation, &self.state)
    }
}

/// The Log Service — owns the log domain state (Phases 7F.1–7F.3; the

/// (including its persisted state), and a `Request` carrying `Inspect`
/// answers with the state summary. The Phase 7F.1 proof behavior is

/// The Storage Service — owns the storage domain boundary (Phase 7F.3,
/// Phase 7G boundary, Phase 7G.1 live wiring).
///
/// The Storage Service is a **platform service**: it owns the real storage
/// stack behind the platform boundary — the [`Syss`] storage space over the
/// platform storage root, the [`Pss`] serialization service and the
/// [`Recovery`] crash-recovery service — and performs the real storage
/// operations through them. Operations: `Save` stores an artifact (validated
/// and serialized by PSS, written by Syss), `Load` reads and deserializes an
/// entry back, `Recover` runs crash recovery over the root, `Probe` performs
/// the platform-storage capability probe, and a `Request` carrying `Inspect`
/// answers with the deterministic storage-stack summary.
///
/// The architectural boundary is `StorageAuthority → StorageService → Syss
/// (storage space) / Pss (serialization) / Recovery (crash recovery) →
/// `ra-persistence` (codec layer) → persistent storage`. The service
/// implements no persistence: it calls the existing stack, and the
/// `ra-persistence` codec architecture, PSS and Recovery are untouched.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct StorageService {
    core: ServiceCore,
    state: RefCell<StorageState>,
}

impl StorageService {
    /// Creates the Storage Service, owned by the Storage Authority, over the
    /// platform default storage root (Phase 7G.1).
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`StorageService::with_root`] with the resolved platform root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> StorageService {
        Self::with_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the Storage Service over the given storage root.
    ///
    /// The additive root-bound constructor: the boot chain
    /// ([`crate::SySS`](crate::SySS::initialize_with_storage_root)) threads
    /// the resolved platform storage root down to the Storage Authority, and
    /// the tests use it for isolation.
    pub(crate) fn with_root(root: PathBuf) -> StorageService {
        StorageService {
            core: ServiceCore::new(ServiceId::new("storage"), HubId::STORAGE),
            state: RefCell::new(StorageState::new(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl Service for StorageService {
    fn core(&self) -> &ServiceCore {
        &self.core
    }

    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
        invoke_storage(invocation, &self.state)
    }
}

/// The Device Service — owns the device domain boundary (Phase 7F.3).
///
/// The Device Service is a **platform boundary only**: it maintains the
/// minimal device/platform capability state and performs a deterministic
/// capability probe. Operations: `Probe` performs the probe and a `Request`
/// carrying `Inspect` answers with the capability. It performs **no** real
/// hardware/device I/O — no drivers, no networking, no USB, no filesystem
/// device drivers and no OS kernel calls.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct DeviceService {
    core: ServiceCore,
    state: RefCell<ProbeState>,
}

impl DeviceService {
    /// Creates the Device Service, owned by the Device Authority, with the
    /// platform device capability.
    pub(crate) fn new() -> DeviceService {
        DeviceService {
            core: ServiceCore::new(ServiceId::new("device"), HubId::DEVICE),
            state: RefCell::new(ProbeState::new(
                "platform device abstraction — no hardware I/O",
            )),
        }
    }
}

impl Service for DeviceService {
    fn core(&self) -> &ServiceCore {
        &self.core
    }

    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
        invoke_probe(invocation, || self.state.borrow().summary("device"))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn log_request() -> BackboneMessage {
        BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        )
    }

    /// Builds a message from `source` to `target` carrying `operation`.
    fn message(
        kind: BackboneMessageKind,
        source: HubId,
        target: HubId,
        operation: ServiceOperation,
    ) -> BackboneMessage {
        BackboneMessage::new(kind, source, Some(target))
            .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(operation))
    }

    /// Invokes `service` with the given kind/operation/target and returns the
    /// resulting [`ServiceResult`].
    fn invoke(
        service: &dyn Service,
        kind: BackboneMessageKind,
        operation: ServiceOperation,
        target: HubId,
    ) -> ServiceResult {
        let message = message(kind, HubId::DEVICE, target, operation);
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        service.invoke(&invocation).unwrap()
    }

    /// All seven Phase 7F.2 domain services as trait objects.
    fn all_domain_services() -> Vec<Box<dyn Service>> {
        vec![
            Box::new(WorkspaceService::new()),
            Box::new(ProjectService::new()),
            Box::new(PackageService::new()),
            Box::new(SettingsService::new()),
            Box::new(HistoryService::new()),
            Box::new(StorageService::new()),
            Box::new(DeviceService::new()),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_have_a_stable_identity() {
        let service = LogService::new();
        assert_eq!(service.id().name(), "log");
        assert_eq!(service.core().id(), &ServiceId::new("log"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn service_identity_prints_stably() {
        assert_eq!(ServiceId::new("log").to_string(), "log");
        assert_eq!(ServiceId::new("workspace").to_string(), "workspace");
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_owned_by_the_log_authority() {
        let service = LogService::new();
        assert_eq!(service.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(service.core().owner(), HubId::LOG);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_service_cannot_belong_to_another_domain() {
        // The Log Service's owner is fixed to the log domain; it can never
        // belong to any other domain.
        let service = LogService::new();
        assert_eq!(service.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        assert_ne!(service.owner(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_ne!(service.owner(), HubId::PROJECT);
        assert_ne!(service.owner(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_ne!(service.owner(), HubId::DEVICE);
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_ready() {
        let service = LogService::new();
        assert!(service.is_ready());
        assert_eq!(service.core().lifecycle(), ServiceLifecycle::Ready);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invocation_exposes_the_message_and_its_kind() {
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(invocation.message(), &message);
        assert_eq!(invocation.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Command);
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_domain_service_has_a_stable_identity_and_owner() {
        let pairs: [(HubId, &str); 7] = [
            (HubId::WORKSPACE, "workspace"),
            (HubId::PROJECT, "project"),
            (HubId::PACKAGE, "package"),
            (HubId::SETTINGS, "settings"),
            (HubId::HISTORY, "history"),
            (HubId::STORAGE, "storage"),
            (HubId::DEVICE, "device"),
        ];
        for (service, (hub, name)) in all_domain_services().into_iter().zip(pairs) {
            assert_eq!(service.owner(), hub, "{name} must be owned by its domain");
            assert_eq!(service.id().name(), name);
            assert!(service.is_ready());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_domain_service_cannot_belong_to_another_domain() {
        let workspace = WorkspaceService::new();
        assert_eq!(workspace.owner(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_ne!(workspace.owner(), HubId::PROJECT);
        assert_ne!(workspace.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        let storage = StorageService::new();
        assert_eq!(storage.owner(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_ne!(storage.owner(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        let device = DeviceService::new();
        assert_eq!(device.owner(), HubId::DEVICE);
        assert_ne!(device.owner(), HubId::STORAGE);
    }

    #[test]
    fn domain_services_perform_the_operation_kind_contract() {
        for service in all_domain_services() {
            let owner = service.owner();
            // A directive performs the minimal domain operation.
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &*service,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                    ServiceOperation::Accept,
                    owner
                ),
                ServiceResult::Completed,
                "{owner}"
            );
            // A question inspects and answers with the state summary (the
            // synchronous Response).
            assert!(
                matches!(
                    invoke(
                        &*service,
                        BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                        ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                        owner
                    ),
                    ServiceResult::Inspected(_)
                ),
                "{owner}"
            );
            // An informational notification is accepted.
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &*service,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
                    ServiceOperation::Accept,
                    owner
                ),
                ServiceResult::Accepted,
                "{owner}"
            );
            // Mismatched kind/operation pairs are invalid invocations.
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &*service,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                    ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                    owner
                ),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "{owner}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &*service,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                    ServiceOperation::Accept,
                    owner
                ),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "{owner}"
            );
            // Non-request kinds are rejected.
            for kind in [
                BackboneMessageKind::Response,
                BackboneMessageKind::Event,
                BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast,
                BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal,
            ] {
                assert_eq!(
                    invoke(&*service, kind, ServiceOperation::Accept, owner),
                    ServiceResult::Rejected,
                    "{owner}: {kind} is not a service request"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn payload_less_messages_fall_back_to_the_kind_operation() {
        let workspace = WorkspaceService::new();
        // A bare command is a directive (accept); a bare request is a
        // question (inspect).
        let command = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ServiceInvocation::new(&command).operation(),
            ServiceOperation::Accept
        );
        let request = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ServiceInvocation::new(&request).operation(),
            ServiceOperation::Inspect
        );
        // Bare messages invoke through the default operation.
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&command)).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert!(
            matches!(
                workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&request)).unwrap(),
                ServiceResult::Inspected(_)
            ),
            "a bare request is answered with the state summary"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_service_opens_closes_and_inspects() {
        let (_dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        // Initial state: no workspace loaded.
        assert!(matches!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected(ref summary) if summary == "workspace: none"
        ));
        // Open the workspace.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Inspect the resulting state.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
        // Close it back to no workspace.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Close,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn project_service_opens_closes_and_inspects() {
        let (_dir, project) = project_service();
        assert!(matches!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected(ref summary) if summary == "project: none"
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-project".to_owned()),
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("project: ra-project".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Close,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("project: none".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_service_updates_and_inspects() {
        let (_dir, settings) = settings_service();
        // Initial state: empty settings.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("settings: (empty)".to_owned())
        );
        // Update a controlled setting.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "theme".to_owned(),
                    value: "dark".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("settings: theme=dark".to_owned())
        );
        // A second setting sorts deterministically in the summary.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "autosave".to_owned(),
                    value: "on".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("settings: autosave=on, theme=dark".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_probes_and_inspects() {
        let storage = StorageService::new();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Probe,
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("storage: stack=syss,pss,recovery; categories=8".to_owned())
        );

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_owns_the_real_storage_stack() {
        // Phase 7G.1: the Storage Service owns the real storage stack — a
        // Syss handle over its storage root, the fully wired Pss codec
        // registry and the Recovery crash-recovery service.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-service-stack");
        let storage = StorageService::with_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        let state = storage.state.borrow();
        assert_eq!(state.root(), dir.path());
        assert!(state.pss.has_serializer(ra_persistence::Format::Ra));
        assert!(state.pss.has_deserializer(ra_persistence::Format::Ra));
        assert_eq!(
            state.summary(),
            "storage: stack=syss,pss,recovery; categories=8"
        );
        drop(state);
        // Storage still rejects operations outside its domain.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("x".to_owned()),
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_saves_and_loads_through_the_real_stack() {
        // Phase 7G.1: Save reaches the existing Syss/Pss stack — the
        // artifact is validated and serialized by PSS and stored by Syss;
        // Load reads it back through the same stack.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-service-roundtrip");
        let storage = StorageService::with_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        let artifact = Artifact::Program(ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("main.ra", "let x = 1;"));
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Save {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                    artifact,
                },
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // The entry exists in the storage space under the artifact category
        // with the PSS `.ra` serialization.
        let stored = std::fs::read(dir.path().join("artifacts/main.ra")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored, b"let x = 1;");
        // Load returns the loaded representation through the same stack.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Loaded("loaded main.ra: program: let x = 1;".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_loads_missing_entries_as_rejections() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-service-missing");
        let storage = StorageService::with_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        // A missing entry is a deterministic storage failure: the service
        // rejects the Load (the transport succeeded, storage did not).
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "missing.ra".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_rejects_unsafe_storage_names() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-service-names");
        let storage = StorageService::with_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        let artifact = Artifact::Program(ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("main.ra", "x"));
        for bad in ["", ".", "..", "a/b", "a\\b", "nul", "com1.txt"] {
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &storage,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                    ServiceOperation::Save {
                        category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                        name: bad.to_owned(),
                        artifact: artifact.clone(),
                    },
                    HubId::STORAGE
                ),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "name {bad:?} accepted"
            );
        }
        // A name without a supported format extension cannot be loaded.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "no-extension".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_service_recover_resolves_interrupted_writes() {
        // Phase 7G.1: Recover reaches the existing Recovery service — an
        // interrupted atomic write (a `*.ra-tmp` sibling) is rolled forward
        // to its final name.
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7g1-service-recover");
        let storage = StorageService::with_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("main.ra.ra-tmp"), b"let x = 1;").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Recover,
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Recovered(
                "recovery: scanned=1, restored=1, removed=0, failed=0".to_owned()
            )
        );
        // The interrupted write was rolled forward to its final name.
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(dir.path().join("main.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let x = 1;"
        );
        assert!(!dir.path().join("main.ra.ra-tmp").exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn storage_operations_are_rejected_outside_the_storage_domain() {
        // Save / Load / Recover belong to the storage domain: a non-storage
        // service rejects them deterministically.
        let workspace = WorkspaceService::new();
        let artifact = Artifact::Program(ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("main.ra", "x"));
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Save {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                    artifact,
                },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Load {
                    category: StorageCategory::Artifact,
                    name: "main.ra".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Recover,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn operations_are_rejected_outside_their_domain() {
        // A real operation outside the domain is an invalid invocation: the
        // owning service rejects it deterministically.
        let workspace = WorkspaceService::new();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "theme".to_owned(),
                    value: "dark".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        let (_dir, settings) = settings_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        let (_dir, history) = history_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &history,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Probe,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        let device = DeviceService::new();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &device,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Close,
                HubId::DEVICE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        let storage = StorageService::new();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &storage,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Record("x".to_owned()),
                HubId::STORAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn domain_state_is_isolated_across_services() {
        // Services carry their state privately and hold no reference to any
        // other service: opening the workspace cannot touch the project, and
        // recording history cannot touch the log or the settings.
        let (_ws_dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        let (_pr_dir, project) = project_service();
        let (_hi_dir, history) = history_service();
        let (_lo_dir, log) = log_service();
        let (_se_dir, settings) = settings_service();

        invoke(
            &workspace,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("open workspace".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        invoke(
            &settings,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Set {
                key: "theme".to_owned(),
                value: "dark".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::SETTINGS,
        );

        // The other domains are untouched.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("project: none".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("log: 0 entries".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &history,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("history: 1 entries [open workspace]".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_service_answers_a_question_with_its_state() {
        let (_dir, service) = log_service();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        // A question is answered with the inspection of the log state (the
        // synchronous Response path).
        assert_eq!(
            service.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("log: 0 entries".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_service_rejects_non_log_requests() {
        let service = LogService::new();
        for kind in [
            BackboneMessageKind::Response,
            BackboneMessageKind::Event,
            BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast,
            BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal,
        ] {
            let message = BackboneMessage::new(kind, HubId::DEVICE, Some(HubId::LOG));
            let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
            assert_eq!(
                service.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "{kind} is not a log request"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn service_results_are_distinct() {
        assert_ne!(ServiceResult::Accepted, ServiceResult::Completed);
        assert_ne!(ServiceResult::Completed, ServiceResult::Rejected);
        assert_ne!(ServiceResult::Accepted, ServiceResult::Rejected);
        assert_ne!(
            ServiceResult::Inspected("a".to_owned()),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("b".to_owned())
        );
        assert_ne!(
            ServiceResult::Inspected("a".to_owned()),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_duplicate_open_is_rejected() {
        let (_dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Phase 7H: opening an already-open workspace is rejected by the
        // validated lifecycle — deterministically, never a panic.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(

                ServiceOperation::Open("other".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

                    name: "ra-lib".to_owned(),

        (dir, service)
    }

    }

        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-package");

        (dir, service)
    }

    /// A workspace service over the same storage root as `dir` — the reopen

        WorkspaceService::with_root(dir.path().join("store"))

    /// The full path of a persisted entry under the service's storage root.
    fn stored_entry(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        category: StorageCategory,
        name: &str,
    ) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        dir.join("store").join(category.dir_name()).join(name)
    }

    /// Decodes the persisted state text of an entry through the existing
    /// `.ra` text codec.
    fn persisted_state(dir: &std::path::Path, category: StorageCategory, name: &str) -> String {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(stored_entry(dir, category, name)).unwrap();
        Pss::new()
            .deserialize_program(ra_persistence::Format::Ra, &bytes)
            .unwrap()
            .text()
            .to_owned()
    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_open_persists_its_state() {
        let (dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // The workspace state is persisted atomically into `workspaces/`
        // through the existing `.ra` text codec.
        assert_eq!(
            persisted_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Workspace, "ra-main"),
            "workspace: ra-main"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_close_preserves_persisted_state_and_reopen_restores_it() {
        let (dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        invoke(
            &workspace,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Close,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Closing does not delete the persisted state.
        assert!(stored_entry(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Workspace, "ra-main").is_file());
        // A fresh service over the same root reopens the workspace.
        let reopened = workspace_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &reopened,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &reopened,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_reopen_restores_the_identity() {
        let (dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        invoke(
            &workspace,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );

            HubId::WORKSPACE,

    }

    #[test]
    fn workspace_open_rejects_corrupt_persisted_state() {
        let (dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        // A persisted entry that cannot be decoded through the codec is
        // rejected deterministically.
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("store/workspaces")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            stored_entry(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Workspace, "ra-main"),
            b"\xff\xfe not utf-8",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // A persisted entry of the wrong kind (or a mismatched name) is also
        // rejected.
        let (dir2, workspace2) = workspace_service();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir2.path().join("store/workspaces")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            stored_entry(dir2.path(), StorageCategory::Workspace, "ra-main"),
            b"project: ra-main",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace2,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupted_persisted_writes_are_recovered() {
        // An interrupted atomic write leaves a `*.ra-tmp` sibling; the
        // existing Recovery service resolves it (rolls it forward when no
        // final file exists, removes it as stale otherwise).
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-recovery");
        let store = dir.path().join("store");
        // Workspace: an interrupted write is rolled forward.
        std::fs::create_dir_all(store.join("workspaces")).unwrap();
        let pss = Pss::new();
        let bytes = pss
            .serialize_program(
                ra_persistence::Format::Ra,
                &ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("ra-main", "workspace: ra-main"),
            )
            .unwrap();
        std::fs::write(store.join("workspaces/ra-main.ra-tmp"), &bytes).unwrap();
        // Project: same, with an association.
        std::fs::create_dir_all(store.join("projects")).unwrap();
        let bytes = pss
            .serialize_program(
                ra_persistence::Format::Ra,
                &ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("ra-lib", "project: ra-lib\nin: ra-main"),
            )
            .unwrap();
        std::fs::write(store.join("projects/ra-lib.ra-tmp"), &bytes).unwrap();
        // Package: same.
        std::fs::create_dir_all(store.join("packages")).unwrap();
        let bytes = pss
            .serialize_program(
                ra_persistence::Format::Ra,
                &ra_persistence::LiveProgram::new("ra-pkg", "package: ra-pkg\nin: ra-lib"),
            )
            .unwrap();
        std::fs::write(store.join("packages/ra-pkg.ra-tmp"), &bytes).unwrap();
        // The existing recovery mechanism resolves every interrupted write.
        let report = Recovery::new().recover(&store).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report.scanned, 3);
        assert_eq!(report.restored.len(), 3);
        assert!(report.failed.is_empty());
        // The recovered state is reopenable through the normal open path.
        let workspace = workspace_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &workspace,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let project = project_service_in(&dir);
        invoke(
            &project,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-lib".to_owned()),
            HubId::PROJECT,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("project: ra-lib in ra-main".to_owned())
        );
        let package = package_service_in(&dir);
        invoke(
            &package,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-pkg".to_owned()),
            HubId::PACKAGE,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &package,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::PACKAGE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("package: ra-pkg in ra-lib".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn stale_temp_with_existing_final_is_removed_by_recovery() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-recovery-stale");
        let store = dir.path().join("store");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(store.join("workspaces")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(store.join("workspaces/ra-main"), b"committed").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(store.join("workspaces/ra-main.ra-tmp"), b"older attempt").unwrap();
        let report = Recovery::new().recover(&store).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report.scanned, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.removed.len(), 1);
        assert!(report.restored.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(store.join("workspaces/ra-main")).unwrap(),
            b"committed"
        );
        assert!(!store.join("workspaces/ra-main.ra-tmp").exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_object_persistence_stays_inside_the_storage_root() {
        // Opening and persisting workspace/project/package objects writes
        // only into their own categories under the storage root — no
        // arbitrary filesystem access outside Syss.
        let (dir, workspace) = workspace_service();
        let project = project_service_in(&dir);
        let package = package_service_in(&dir);
        invoke(
            &workspace,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        invoke(
            &project,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::OpenIn {
                name: "ra-lib".to_owned(),
                parent: "ra-main".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::PROJECT,
        );
        invoke(
            &package,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::OpenIn {
                name: "ra-pkg".to_owned(),
                parent: "ra-lib".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::PACKAGE,
        );
        // The persisted entries live only under their categories.
        assert!(stored_entry(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Workspace, "ra-main").is_file());
        assert!(stored_entry(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Project, "ra-lib").is_file());
        assert!(stored_entry(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Package, "ra-pkg").is_file());
        // No other category was written by the active-object domains.
        for category in StorageCategory::ALL {
            let dir_path = dir.path().join("store").join(category.dir_name());
            if matches!(
                category,
                StorageCategory::Workspace | StorageCategory::Project | StorageCategory::Package
            ) {
                assert!(dir_path.is_dir(), "{category} dir missing");
            } else {
                assert!(
                    !dir_path.exists(),
                    "{category} dir was created unexpectedly"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    /// The path of a persisted platform-state file under the service root.
    fn stored_platform_state(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        category: StorageCategory,
        name: &str,
    ) -> std::path::PathBuf {
