    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_have_deterministic_defaults() {
        let (_dir, settings) = settings_service();
        // The known settings have deterministic defaults even when never set.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("light".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("view".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("editor".to_owned())
        );
        // An unknown setting has no value.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("nope".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_update_persists_and_retrieves() {
        let (dir, settings) = settings_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "theme".to_owned(),
                    value: "dark".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // The value is retrievable and persisted as one file per key.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("dark".to_owned())
        );
        assert!(stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Settings, "theme").is_file());
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_reject_invalid_updates() {
        let (_dir, settings) = settings_service();
        // Unsupported values for a fixed-set setting are rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "theme".to_owned(),
                    value: "blue".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // Invalid keys and values are rejected deterministically.
        for bad in ["", ".", "a/b"] {
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &settings,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                    ServiceOperation::Set {
                        key: bad.to_owned(),
                        value: "x".to_owned(),
                    },
                    HubId::SETTINGS
                ),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "key {bad:?} accepted"
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "autosave".to_owned(),
                    value: "".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Set {
                    key: "autosave".to_owned(),
                    value: "a\nb".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // No invalid value was persisted.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("settings: (empty)".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_persist_and_restore_after_restart() {
        let (dir, settings) = settings_service();
        invoke(
            &settings,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Set {
                key: "theme".to_owned(),
                value: "dark".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::SETTINGS,
        );
        invoke(
            &settings,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Set {
                key: "autosave".to_owned(),
                value: "on".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::SETTINGS,
        );
        // A fresh service over the same root restores the persisted values.
        let restored = settings_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("settings: autosave=on, theme=dark".to_owned())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("dark".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_corrupt_persisted_state_is_rejected() {
        let (dir, settings) = settings_service();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("store/settings")).unwrap();
        // A persisted value that cannot be decoded through the codec fails
        // the settings load deterministically.
        std::fs::write(
            stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Settings, "theme"),
            b"\xff\xfe not utf-8",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Get("theme".to_owned()),
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &settings,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::SETTINGS
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_persistence_stays_inside_the_storage_root() {
        let (dir, settings) = settings_service();
        invoke(
            &settings,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Set {
                key: "theme".to_owned(),
                value: "dark".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::SETTINGS,
        );
        // The settings write lives only under the `settings/` category.
        assert!(stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Settings, "theme").is_file());
        for category in StorageCategory::ALL {
            let dir_path = dir.path().join("store").join(category.dir_name());
            if category == StorageCategory::Settings {
                assert!(dir_path.is_dir(), "{category} dir missing");
            } else {
                assert!(
                    !dir_path.exists(),
                    "{category} dir was created unexpectedly"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_records_in_order_and_persists() {
        let (dir, history) = history_service();
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("open workspace ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("save document".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        // Ordering is the record order, and the state is persisted.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &history,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected(
                "history: 2 entries [open workspace ra-main, save document]".to_owned()
            )
        );
        assert!(stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::History, "history").is_file());
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_restores_its_entries_after_restart() {
        let (dir, history) = history_service();
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("open workspace ra-main".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("save document".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        let restored = history_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected(
                "history: 2 entries [open workspace ra-main, save document]".to_owned()
            )
        );
        // Appending after restore keeps the order.
        invoke(
            &restored,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("close document".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected(
                "history: 3 entries [open workspace ra-main, save document, close document]"
                    .to_owned()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_clear_removes_the_persisted_state() {
        let (dir, history) = history_service();
        invoke(
            &history,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("open workspace".to_owned()),
            HubId::HISTORY,
        );

                ServiceOperation::Inspect,

        // The persisted file is gone, so a restart also starts empty.
        assert!(!stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::History, "history").exists());

        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::HISTORY
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("history: 0 entries".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_records_structured_entries() {
        let (_dir, log) = log_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                    severity: LogSeverity::Warning,
                    source: "workspace".to_owned(),
                    message: "disk nearly full".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // The record carries its deterministic sequence, severity, source and
        // message; the summary lists the messages (back-compatible).
        let state = log.state.borrow();
        let record = &state.records[0];
        assert_eq!(record.sequence(), 1);
        assert_eq!(record.severity(), LogSeverity::Warning);
        assert_eq!(record.source(), "workspace");
        assert_eq!(record.message(), "disk nearly full");
        drop(state);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("log: 1 entries [disk nearly full]".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_record_messages_are_backward_compatible() {
        let (_dir, log) = log_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Record("platform ready".to_owned()),
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("log: 1 entries [platform ready]".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_persists_and_restores_structured_records_after_restart() {
        let (dir, log) = log_service();
        invoke(
            &log,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                severity: LogSeverity::Error,
                source: "storage".to_owned(),
                message: "write failed".to_owned(),
            },
            HubId::LOG,
        );
        invoke(
            &log,
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            ServiceOperation::Record("platform ready".to_owned()),
            HubId::LOG,
        );
        // A fresh service over the same root restores the structured records
        // with their severity, source and deterministic order. Loading is
        // lazy, so the first operation triggers the load.
        let restored = log_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &restored,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("log: 2 entries [write failed, platform ready]".to_owned())
        );
        {
            let state = restored.state.borrow();
            assert_eq!(state.records.len(), 2);
            assert_eq!(state.records[0].severity(), LogSeverity::Error);
            assert_eq!(state.records[0].source(), "storage");
            assert_eq!(state.records[0].message(), "write failed");
            assert_eq!(state.records[1].severity(), LogSeverity::Info);
            assert_eq!(state.records[1].source(), "log");
            assert_eq!(state.records[1].message(), "platform ready");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_rejects_invalid_records() {
        let (_dir, log) = log_service();
        // A source with whitespace cannot be persisted as a line token.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                    severity: LogSeverity::Info,
                    source: "".to_owned(),
                    message: "x".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // A message with a line break cannot be persisted as one line.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::RecordLog {
                    severity: LogSeverity::Info,
                    source: "workspace".to_owned(),
                    message: "a\nb".to_owned(),
                },
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                ServiceOperation::Record("".to_owned()),
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_corrupt_persisted_state_is_rejected() {
        let (dir, log) = log_service();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("store/logs")).unwrap();
        // Undecodable bytes are rejected.
        std::fs::write(
            stored_platform_state(dir.path(), StorageCategory::Logs, "log"),
            b"\xff\xfe not utf-8",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // A structurally unparsable line is also corrupt state.
        let (dir2, log2) = log_service();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir2.path().join("store/logs")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            stored_platform_state(dir2.path(), StorageCategory::Logs, "log"),
            b"not a valid log line",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &log2,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::Inspect,
                HubId::LOG
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_clear_removes_the_persisted_state() {
        let (dir, log) = log_service();
        invoke(
            &log,

            ServiceOperation::Record("platform ready".to_owned()),
            HubId::LOG,

        assert_eq!(
            invoke(

                ServiceOperation::Clear,
                HubId::LOG

        let restored = log_service_in(&dir);
        assert_eq!(

        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn log_service_remains_owned_by_the_log_authority() {
        // Phase 7H.2: the log service is still bound to the Log Authority —
        // the ownership chain `LogAuthority → LogService` is untouched.
        let (_dir, service) = log_service();
        assert_eq!(service.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(service.core().owner(), HubId::LOG);
    }

    // ── Phase 7H: document operations ─────────────────────────

    /// A document service over an isolated storage root: `store` under the
    /// temp dir holds the platform storage, `device` holds the device files
    /// the operations read from and write to.
    fn document_service() -> (crate::test_support::TempDir, WorkspaceService) {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h-document");
        let service = WorkspaceService::with_root(dir.path().join("store"));
        (dir, service)
    }

    /// Writes a device file under the `device` directory and returns its
    /// path.
    fn write_device_file(dir: &std::path::Path, name: &str, content: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        let device = dir.join("device");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&device).unwrap();
        let path = device.join(name);
        std::fs::write(&path, content).unwrap();
        path
    }

    /// The stored file of a document in the platform's files category.
    fn stored_document(dir: &std::path::Path, name: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        dir.join("store").join("files").join(name)
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_open_loads_a_device_file_as_the_active_document() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Opened("opened main.ra".to_owned())
        );
        // The document is the active document and reads its current state.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("document: main.ra: let x = 1;".to_owned())
        );
        // The device file was brought into the platform's files category
        // through the existing stack (Device File → SySS).
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(stored_document(dir.path(), "main.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let x = 1;"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_inspect_reports_none_when_closed() {
        let (_dir, service) = document_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("document: none".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_duplicate_open_is_rejected() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument {
                    source: source.clone()
                },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Opened("opened main.ra".to_owned())
        );
        // Opening an already-open document is rejected by the lifecycle.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]

        assert_eq!(
            invoke(

            ),

        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_save_persists_the_current_content() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        invoke(
            &service,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        // Modify the current state, then save: the persisted content is the
        // modified content — save is real, not a re-write of the loaded
        // bytes.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::SetDocumentContent("let y = 2;".to_owned()),
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(stored_document(dir.path(), "main.ra")).unwrap(),
            b"let y = 2;"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("document: main.ra: let y = 2;".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn document_open_rejects_path_traversal_and_invalid_names() {
        let (_dir, service) = document_service();
        // Names that cannot be derived from a usable file name, or that fail
        // the platform name validation, are rejected — no path traversal can
        // reach the storage space.
        for bad in ["..", ".", ""] {
            assert_eq!(
                invoke(
                    &service,
                    BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                    ServiceOperation::OpenDocument {
                        source: std::path::PathBuf::from(bad),
                    },
                    HubId::WORKSPACE
                ),
                ServiceResult::Rejected,
                "path {bad:?} accepted"
            );
        }
        // A device path whose file name is a reserved device name is rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument {
                    source: std::path::PathBuf::from("nul.ra"),
                },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_open_rejects_unsupported_formats() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        // A device file whose name has no supported codec extension cannot be
        // opened — there is no codec to deserialize it with.
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "notes.txt", "hello");
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        // Binary formats report pending encodings at the codec layer, so a
        // binary open is honestly rejected.
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.rab", "whatever");
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_close_returns_to_none() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        invoke(
            &service,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::CloseDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &service,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::InspectDocument,
                HubId::WORKSPACE
            ),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("document: none".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_persistence_stays_inside_the_storage_root() {
        let (dir, service) = document_service();
        let source = write_device_file(dir.path(), "main.ra", "let x = 1;");
        invoke(
            &service,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::OpenDocument { source },
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        invoke(
            &service,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        let second = write_device_file(dir.path(), "second.ra", "let y = 1;");
        invoke(
            &service,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            ServiceOperation::ImportDocument { source: second },
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
        );
        // The storage writes live only under the files category inside the
        // platform root — no arbitrary filesystem access outside Syss.
        assert!(stored_document(dir.path(), "main.ra").is_file());
        assert!(stored_document(dir.path(), "second.ra").is_file());
        // No category other than files was written by the document domain.
        for category in StorageCategory::ALL {
            let dir_path = dir.path().join("store").join(category.dir_name());
            if category == StorageCategory::LoadedFile {
                assert!(dir_path.is_dir(), "{category} dir missing");
            } else {
                assert!(
                    !dir_path.exists(),
                    "{category} dir was created unexpectedly"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_operations_are_rejected_outside_the_workspace_domain() {
        // Document operations belong to the workspace domain: a non-workspace
        // service rejects them deterministically.
        let (_dir, project) = project_service();
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::OpenDocument {
                    source: std::path::PathBuf::from("main.ra"),
                },
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            invoke(
                &project,
                BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                ServiceOperation::SaveDocument,
                HubId::PROJECT
            ),
            ServiceResult::Rejected
        );
    }
}

=== AUTHORITY IMPLEMENTATIONS ===
//! Hub authorities (Phase 7D.2).
//!
//! The **hub authority** is the concrete, per-domain ownership object of the
//! Platform Kernel. Phase 7D.1 defined the hub **contracts** — the static
//! [`Hub`] metadata, the [`HubDomain`] vocabulary, the stable [`HubId`]s and
//! the [`HubLifecycle`] states. Phase 7D.2 turns those contracts into the
//! eight concrete authorities the kernel will run on:
//!
//! * [`WorkspaceAuthority`] — owns the workspace domain;
//! * [`ProjectAuthority`] — owns the project domain;
//! * [`PackageAuthority`] — owns the package domain;
//! * [`SettingsAuthority`] — owns the settings domain;
//! * [`HistoryAuthority`] — owns the history domain;
//! * [`LogAuthority`] — owns the log domain;
//! * [`StorageAuthority`] — owns the storage domain;
//! * [`DeviceAuthority`] — owns the device domain.
//!
//! Every authority:
//!
//! * owns **exactly one platform domain** (its type fixes its domain — a
//!   [`WorkspaceAuthority`] can never own anything but the workspace domain);
//! * **composes the hub metadata** ([`Hub`]) — the static id/domain pair the
//!   authority is the owner of;
//! * **exposes its lifecycle state** ([`HubLifecycle`]);
//! * **acknowledges backbone delivery** through a controlled delivery
//!   boundary ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) — the only way a message reaches an
//!   authority (Phase 7E.1);
//! * **owns its services** — reached through a controlled service boundary
//!   ([`HubAuthority::service`], [`HubAuthority::invoke`]): every authority
//!   owns the service of its domain, and invocation forwards platform
//!   requests to the owned service (Phases 7F.1–7F.2);
//! * **supports registration** with the hub [`Registry`] (delegated from the
//!   authority; the registration *orchestration* is Phase 7D.3);
//! * exposes **no domain operations** (no save, load, compile or run);
//! * contains **no business logic**.
//!
//! # Lifecycle state placement
//!
//! Phase 7D.1 left the placement of per-hub lifecycle state open. Phase 7D.2
//! decides: the lifecycle state lives **on the authority** (this module), not
//! on the static [`Hub`] metadata. Authorities are born
//! [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] — the first state of the documented chain
//! (`Registered → Initialized → Active ⇄ Suspended → Shutdown`).
//!
//! Phase 7D.3 implements the **startup transitions**; Phase 7F.5 completes
//! the lifecycle:
//!
//! * [`HubAuthority::initialize`] — `Registered → Initialized`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::activate`] — `Initialized → Active`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::suspend`] — `Active → Suspended`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::resume`] — `Suspended → Active`;
//! * [`HubAuthority::shutdown`] — `Active | Suspended → Shutdown`.
//!
//! Every named transition delegates to the **single validated transition
//! mechanism** ([`HubAuthority::transition`]), which applies the one
//! transition table ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]); transition logic is
//! never duplicated across authorities. Suspension **preserves** domain
//! state (pause, not shutdown); shutdown is terminal. The aggregate
//! platform control lives on the Platform Kernel (the `kernel` module), the
//! owner of aggregate lifecycle control.
//!
//! # Authority ownership
//!
//! The ownership chain of each platform domain is fixed:
//!
//! `Authority → State → Services → Events → Policies`
//!
//! The authority owns exactly one domain and owns that domain's **state**,
//! **services**, **events** and **policies**. **Services never own
//! authorities** — an authority owns its services, never the other way
//! around. The Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) dispatches to
//! authorities; services are reached through their owning authority, never
//! directly.
//!
//! # Scope
//!
//! Phase 7E.1: authorities are ownership objects with one addition — the
//! controlled backbone **delivery boundary** ([`HubAuthority::receive`]),
//! which acknowledges receipt without doing any work. Phase 7F.1 adds the
//! controlled **service boundary** ([`HubAuthority::service`],
//! [`HubAuthority::invoke`]). Phase 7F.2 binds every authority to the
//! service of its domain. Phase 7F.3: the services behind the boundary own
//! real domain state and perform real domain operations — the authority
//! remains the domain owner and forwards requests to its owned service, and
//! the frozen kernel ownership is untouched.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use super::backbone::{BackboneMessage, DeliveryReceipt};
use super::service::{
    DeviceService, HistoryService, LogService, PackageService, ProjectService, Service,
    ServiceInvocation, ServiceResult, SettingsService, StorageService, WorkspaceService,
};
use super::{Hub, HubDomain, HubError, HubId, HubLifecycle, HubResult, Registry};

/// The authoritative ownership contract of a single platform domain.
///
/// Implemented by every concrete hub authority. The trait exposes the
/// authority's identity, its composed hub metadata and its lifecycle state —
/// nothing more. It deliberately exposes **no domain operations**.
pub(crate) trait HubAuthority {
    /// Returns the stable identifier of this authority in the hub graph.
    fn id(&self) -> HubId;

    /// Returns the platform domain this authority owns.
    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain;

    /// Returns the composed hub metadata (the static id/domain pair).
    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub;

    /// Returns the current lifecycle state of this authority.
    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle;

    /// Sets the authority's lifecycle state.
    ///
    /// Storage primitive backing the validated default transitions
    /// ([`HubAuthority::transition`]); concrete authorities implement it by
    /// writing their own lifecycle field. **Not** a transition by itself —
    /// callers must go through the validated transition mechanism.
    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle);

    /// The single validated lifecycle transition mechanism (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Validates `self`'s current state against `to` using the one
    /// transition table ([`HubLifecycle::can_transition`]) and applies the
    /// transition when it is allowed. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] otherwise. Every named transition
    /// (`initialize`, `activate`, `suspend`, `resume`, `shutdown`)
    /// delegates here — transition logic is never duplicated across
    /// authorities.
    fn transition(&mut self, to: HubLifecycle) -> HubResult<()> {
        let from = self.lifecycle();
        if !from.can_transition(to) {
            return Err(HubError::InvalidTransition { from, to });
        }
        self.set_lifecycle(to);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Startup transition: `Registered → Initialized`.
    ///
    /// Fails with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// in the [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] state.
    fn initialize(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Initialized)
    }

    /// Startup transition: `Initialized → Active`.
    ///
    /// Fails with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// in the [`HubLifecycle::Initialized`] state.
    fn activate(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Active)
    }

    /// Suspension transition: `Active → Suspended` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// A suspended authority is **paused, not shut down**: it is never
    /// routed to, its services are unavailable for normal execution, and its
    /// domain state is preserved for a later [`HubAuthority::resume`]. Fails
    /// with [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`].
    fn suspend(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Suspended)
    }

    /// Resume transition: `Suspended → Active` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Restores an authority suspended by [`HubAuthority::suspend`]; the
    /// domain state preserved during suspension remains available and the
    /// authority is routed to again. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is not
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Suspended`].
    fn resume(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Active)
    }

    /// Shutdown transition: `Active | Suspended → Shutdown` (Phase 7F.5).
    ///
    /// Terminates the authority: it is never routed to again and its
    /// services can never execute again. [`HubLifecycle::Shutdown`] is
    /// terminal — no transition out of it exists. Fails with
    /// [`HubError::InvalidTransition`] when the authority is neither
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`] nor [`HubLifecycle::Suspended`].
    fn shutdown(&mut self) -> HubResult<()> {
        self.transition(HubLifecycle::Shutdown)
    }

    /// Registers this authority with `registry` under its hub id.
    ///
    /// Delegates to [`Registry::register`] with the authority's composed hub
    /// metadata; fails with
    /// [`crate::hub::HubError::AlreadyRegistered`] when the id is taken.
    /// This is the per-authority registration capability only — registering
    /// the full set of authorities and activating them is the Phase 7D.3
    /// orchestration.
    fn register(&self, registry: &mut Registry) -> HubResult<()> {
        registry.register(*self.hub())
    }

    /// The controlled backbone **delivery boundary**.
    ///
    /// Called **only** by the Platform Backbone (the `backbone` module) when
    /// a message is delivered to this authority; the authority acknowledges
    /// receipt with a [`DeliveryReceipt`] that **is** the delivery result the
    /// backbone returns. The backbone is the single communication path of the
    /// platform — callers must never bypass it.
    ///
    /// The returned receipt describes this single authority's acknowledgment
    /// (recipients `1`); a platform-wide broadcast aggregates the per-authority
    /// acknowledgments into one receipt on the backbone side.
    ///
    /// Phase 7E.1: the default acknowledgment performs no work and exposes no
    /// internal state. Service invocation happens through the controlled
    /// invocation boundary ([`HubAuthority::invoke`]), which acknowledges
    /// delivery through this method; full domain work arrives with the
    /// services of Phase 7F.2.
    fn receive(&self, message: &BackboneMessage) -> DeliveryReceipt {
        DeliveryReceipt::delivered(message, 1)
    }

    /// Returns the service owned by this authority, if any.
    ///
    /// The controlled service-ownership surface: callers observe the owned
    /// service through this accessor only — there is no arbitrary mutable
    /// service collection to reach into. Phase 7F.2: every built-in
    /// authority owns the service of its domain; a service never belongs to
    /// another domain.
    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        None
    }

    /// The controlled service invocation boundary — the `Authority →
    /// Service` step of the communication path
    /// (`PlatformInterface → Backbone → Authority → Service →
    /// ServiceResult`).
    ///
    /// Called with the platform request the authority forwards to the
    /// service it owns. Contract:
    ///
    /// 1. the authority must be [`HubLifecycle::Active`] — a service must
    ///    not be reachable before its owning authority is Active, while it
    ///    is Suspended, or after it is Shutdown
    ///    ([`HubError::InactiveTarget`]);
    /// 2. delivery is acknowledged through the controlled delivery boundary
    ///    ([`HubAuthority::receive`]) — the boundary is never bypassed;
    /// 3. the authority must own a ready service
    ///    ([`HubError::ServiceUnavailable`]);
    /// 4. the owned service performs the work and returns its
    ///    [`ServiceResult`].
    ///
    /// The Active gate is the single service-availability boundary: a
    /// service executes domain operations only while its owning authority is
    /// Active (Phase 7F.5) — Suspended and Shutdown authorities reject
    /// invocation with [`HubError::InactiveTarget`].
    ///
    /// The invocation **acknowledges delivery itself** (step 2): callers
    /// invoke once — they must not pre-deliver the message through
    /// [`HubAuthority::receive`] and then invoke, or the authority
    /// acknowledges it twice. The invocation is addressed to this authority:
    /// the backbone resolves the target before delivery, and the authority
    /// trusts the backbone-resolved target.
    ///
    /// Phase 7F.2: every built-in authority owns the service of its domain;
    /// the [`HubError::ServiceUnavailable`] branch remains defensive for
    /// authorities that own no service.
    fn invoke(&self, invocation: &ServiceInvocation) -> HubResult<ServiceResult> {
        // 1. Active gate — inactive authorities never invoke services.
        if self.lifecycle() != HubLifecycle::Active {
            return Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(self.id()));
        }
        // 2. Delivery acknowledgment through the controlled boundary.
        let _ = self.receive(invocation.message());
        // 3. The owned service performs the domain work: it must be present
        //    and ready, and it must belong to this authority's domain — a
        //    service never belongs to another domain.
        let service = self
            .service()
            .ok_or(HubError::ServiceUnavailable(self.id()))?;
        if service.owner() != self.id() || !service.is_ready() {
            return Err(HubError::ServiceUnavailable(self.id()));
        }
        service.invoke(invocation)
    }
}

/// The Workspace Authority — the owner of the workspace domain.
///
/// Owns exactly one domain (workspace), composes the [`Hub`] metadata, is
/// born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], exposes no domain operations and owns
/// the Workspace Service ([`WorkspaceService`], Phase 7F.2; Phase 7H: over
/// the platform storage root — the workspace domain persists its active
/// document and, since Phase 7H.1, its workspace object through the
/// existing Syss/PSS stack).
///
/// The authority is `Debug` only (like the Storage Authority): its service
/// owns the real storage stack, which is not `PartialEq`/`Clone`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct WorkspaceAuthority {
    hub: Hub,
    lifecycle: HubLifecycle,
    service: Option<WorkspaceService>,
}

impl WorkspaceAuthority {
    /// Creates the Workspace Authority, born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] and
    /// owning the Workspace Service over the platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root`] with the resolved platform
    /// root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> WorkspaceAuthority {
        Self::with_storage_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the Workspace Authority owning the Workspace Service over the
    /// given storage root (Phase 7H, additive).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// workspace boundary through this constructor (the workspace domain
    /// persists its active document through the existing Syss/PSS stack);
    /// the no-argument [`WorkspaceAuthority::new`] resolves the platform
    /// default root and remains the frozen construction path.
    pub(crate) fn with_storage_root(root: PathBuf) -> WorkspaceAuthority {
        WorkspaceAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Workspace),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(WorkspaceService::with_root(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl HubAuthority for WorkspaceAuthority {
    fn id(&self) -> HubId {
        self.hub.id()
    }

    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain {
        self.hub.domain()
    }

    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub {
        &self.hub
    }

    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) {
        self.lifecycle = lifecycle;
    }

    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        self.service.as_ref().map(|service| service as &dyn Service)
    }
}

/// [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], exposes no domain operations and owns the
/// Log Service ([`LogService`], Phases 7F.1–7F.3; Phase 7H.2: over the
/// platform storage root — the log domain persists its records through the
/// existing Syss/PSS stack).
///
/// The authority is `Debug` only (like the Workspace/Storage Authorities):
/// its service owns the real storage stack, which is not
/// `PartialEq`/`Clone`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct LogAuthority {
    hub: Hub,
    lifecycle: HubLifecycle,
    service: Option<LogService>,
}

impl LogAuthority {
    /// Creates the Log Authority, born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] and
    /// owning the Log Service over the platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`LogAuthority::with_storage_root`] with the resolved platform root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> LogAuthority {
        Self::with_storage_root(crate::syss::resolve_storage_root())
    }

    /// Creates the Log Authority owning the Log Service over the given
    /// storage root (Phase 7H.2, additive).
    pub(crate) fn with_storage_root(root: PathBuf) -> LogAuthority {
        LogAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Log),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(LogService::with_root(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl HubAuthority for LogAuthority {
    fn id(&self) -> HubId {
        self.hub.id()
    }

    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain {
        self.hub.domain()
    }

    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub {
        &self.hub
    }

    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) {
        self.lifecycle = lifecycle;
    }

    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        self.service.as_ref().map(|service| service as &dyn Service)
    }
}

/// The Storage Authority — the owner of the storage domain.
///
/// Owns exactly one domain (storage), composes the [`Hub`] metadata, is born
/// [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], exposes no domain operations and owns the
/// Storage Service ([`StorageService`], Phase 7F.2; Phase 7G: its domain
/// state represents the existing storage stack; Phase 7G.1: it owns the
/// **real** storage stack — a [`crate::Syss`] handle over the platform
/// storage root, [`crate::Pss`] serialization and [`crate::Recovery`]
/// crash recovery — behind the platform boundary). All platform storage
/// operations stay behind this authority: never `PlatformInterface →
/// ra-persistence`, `PlatformInterface → filesystem` or `Service →
/// Service` bypasses.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct StorageAuthority {
    hub: Hub,
    lifecycle: HubLifecycle,
    service: Option<StorageService>,
}

impl StorageAuthority {
    /// Creates the Storage Authority, born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] and
    /// owning the Storage Service over the platform default storage root.
    ///
    /// The frozen no-argument construction path, preserved for the default
    /// root and exercised by the tests; the boot chain uses
    /// [`StorageAuthority::with_storage_root`] with the resolved platform
    /// root.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn new() -> StorageAuthority {
        StorageAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Storage),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(StorageService::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Creates the Storage Authority owning the Storage Service over the
    /// given storage root (Phase 7G.1, additive).
    ///
    /// The boot chain threads the resolved platform storage root down to the
    /// storage boundary through this constructor; the no-argument
    /// [`StorageAuthority::new`] resolves the platform default root and
    /// remains the frozen construction path.
    pub(crate) fn with_storage_root(root: PathBuf) -> StorageAuthority {
        StorageAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Storage),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(StorageService::with_root(root)),
        }
    }
}

impl HubAuthority for StorageAuthority {
    fn id(&self) -> HubId {
        self.hub.id()
    }

    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain {
        self.hub.domain()
    }

    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub {
        &self.hub
    }

    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) {
        self.lifecycle = lifecycle;
    }

    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        self.service.as_ref().map(|service| service as &dyn Service)
    }
}

/// The Device Authority — the owner of the device domain.
///
/// Owns exactly one domain (device), composes the [`Hub`] metadata, is born
/// [`HubLifecycle::Registered`], exposes no domain operations and owns the
/// Device Service ([`DeviceService`], Phase 7F.2).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct DeviceAuthority {
    hub: Hub,
    lifecycle: HubLifecycle,
    service: Option<DeviceService>,
}

impl DeviceAuthority {
    /// Creates the Device Authority, born [`HubLifecycle::Registered`] and
    /// owning the Device Service.
    pub(crate) fn new() -> DeviceAuthority {
        DeviceAuthority {
            hub: Hub::new(HubDomain::Device),
            lifecycle: HubLifecycle::Registered,
            service: Some(DeviceService::new()),
        }
    }
}

impl HubAuthority for DeviceAuthority {
    fn id(&self) -> HubId {
        self.hub.id()
    }

    fn domain(&self) -> HubDomain {
        self.hub.domain()
    }

    fn hub(&self) -> &Hub {
        &self.hub
    }

    fn lifecycle(&self) -> HubLifecycle {
        self.lifecycle
    }

    fn set_lifecycle(&mut self, lifecycle: HubLifecycle) {
        self.lifecycle = lifecycle;
    }

    fn service(&self) -> Option<&dyn Service> {
        self.service.as_ref().map(|service| service as &dyn Service)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::hub::HubError;

    /// All eight concrete authorities as trait objects.
    fn all_authorities() -> Vec<Box<dyn HubAuthority>> {
        vec![
            Box::new(WorkspaceAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(ProjectAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(PackageAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(SettingsAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(HistoryAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(LogAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(StorageAuthority::new()),
            Box::new(DeviceAuthority::new()),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_authority_owns_exactly_one_domain() {
        let workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(workspace.id(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(workspace.domain(), HubDomain::Workspace);
        assert_eq!(workspace.hub().id(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(workspace.hub().domain(), HubDomain::Workspace);

        let storage = StorageAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(storage.id(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(storage.domain(), HubDomain::Storage);
        assert_eq!(storage.hub().id(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(storage.hub().domain(), HubDomain::Storage);
    }

    #[test]
    fn authorities_mirror_the_initial_hub_set() {
        let authorities = all_authorities();
        assert_eq!(authorities.len(), HubId::ALL.len());

        // Every stable hub id has exactly one authority, and every authority
        // owns exactly one distinct domain.
        //
        // Comparing against `ALL` relies on the derived `Ord` (enum
        // declaration order) matching the declaration order of `ALL`; both
        // follow the same domain vocabulary, so the sorted vectors must equal
        // the constants exactly.
        let mut ids: Vec<HubId> = authorities.iter().map(|a| a.id()).collect();
        ids.sort();
        ids.dedup();
        assert_eq!(ids, HubId::ALL);

        let mut domains: Vec<HubDomain> = authorities.iter().map(|a| a.domain()).collect();
        domains.sort();
        domains.dedup();
        assert_eq!(domains, HubDomain::ALL);

        // id and domain correspond one-to-one for every authority.
        for authority in &authorities {
            assert_eq!(authority.id(), HubId::from_domain(authority.domain()));
            assert_eq!(authority.hub().id(), authority.id());
            assert_eq!(authority.hub().domain(), authority.domain());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn authorities_are_born_registered() {
        assert_eq!(
            WorkspaceAuthority::new().lifecycle(),
            HubLifecycle::Registered
        );
        assert_eq!(
            StorageAuthority::new().lifecycle(),
            HubLifecycle::Registered
        );
        assert_eq!(DeviceAuthority::new().lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn registration_with_the_registry_round_trips() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        WorkspaceAuthority::new().register(&mut registry).unwrap();

        assert!(registry.contains(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        assert_eq!(
            registry.lookup(HubId::WORKSPACE).map(|hub| hub.domain()),
            Some(HubDomain::Workspace)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_registration_is_rejected() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        let settings = SettingsAuthority::new();
        settings.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
        let err = settings.register(&mut registry).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err, HubError::AlreadyRegistered(HubId::SETTINGS));
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_authority_registers_under_its_own_id() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            authority.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for id in HubId::ALL {
            assert!(registry.contains(id));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initialize_transitions_registered_to_initialized() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Registered);
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Initialized);
    }

    #[test]
    fn activate_transitions_initialized_to_active() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_full_startup_chain_reaches_active() {
        for mut authority in all_authorities() {
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn initialize_rejects_a_non_registered_state() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        // Already Initialized: the startup transition must reject it.
        let err = workspace.initialize().unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn activate_rejects_a_non_initialized_state() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        // Still Registered: activation requires Initialized first.
        let err = workspace.activate().unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn startup_chain_runs_after_registration() {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        let mut activated: Vec<Box<dyn HubAuthority>> = all_authorities();
        for authority in activated.iter_mut() {
            authority.register(&mut registry).unwrap();
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(registry.len(), HubId::ALL.len());
        for authority in &activated {
            assert_eq!(authority.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn authorities_acknowledge_backbone_delivery() {
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        let receipt = log.receive(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            receipt.status(),
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneStatus::Delivered
        );
        assert_eq!(
            receipt.kind(),
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Notification
        );
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::DEVICE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::LOG));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    fn log_request() -> crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage {
        crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_authority_owns_the_log_service() {
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let service = log.service().expect("log authority owns the log service");
        assert_eq!(service.id().name(), "log");
        assert_eq!(service.owner(), HubId::LOG);
        assert!(service.is_ready());
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_authority_owns_the_service_of_its_domain() {
        let pairs: [(HubId, &str); 8] = [
            (HubId::WORKSPACE, "workspace"),
            (HubId::PROJECT, "project"),
            (HubId::PACKAGE, "package"),
            (HubId::SETTINGS, "settings"),
            (HubId::HISTORY, "history"),
            (HubId::LOG, "log"),
            (HubId::STORAGE, "storage"),
            (HubId::DEVICE, "device"),
        ];
        for (hub, name) in pairs {
            let authority = all_authorities()
                .into_iter()
                .find(|authority| authority.id() == hub)
                .expect("authority exists");
            let service = authority
                .service()
                .expect("every authority owns the service of its domain");
            assert_eq!(
                service.owner(),
                hub,
                "{name} service must be owned by {hub}"
            );
            assert_eq!(service.id().name(), name);
            assert!(service.is_ready());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_service_never_belongs_to_another_domain() {
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            let service = authority.service().unwrap();
            // The authority's own service belongs to its domain, never to
            // any other domain.
            assert_eq!(service.owner(), authority.id());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_active_authority_invokes_its_owned_service() {
        let mut authorities = all_authorities();
        for authority in authorities.iter_mut() {
            authority.initialize().unwrap();
            authority.activate().unwrap();
        }
        for authority in authorities.iter() {
            let hub = authority.id();
            let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
                crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                HubId::DEVICE,
                Some(hub),
            );
            let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
            // The Log proof service and the domain services both complete a
            // command.
            assert_eq!(
                authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
                ServiceResult::Completed,
                "authority {hub} must invoke its owned service"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_inactive_authority_prevents_service_invocation() {
        // Authorities are born Registered: their services must not be
        // reachable until the authority is Active.
        for authority in all_authorities() {
            let hub = authority.id();
            let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
                crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                HubId::DEVICE,
                Some(hub),
            );
            let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
            assert_eq!(
                authority.invoke(&invocation),
                Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(hub)),
                "authority {hub} must reject invocation while inactive"
            );
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn active_authority_forwards_the_request_to_its_service() {
        let mut log = LogAuthority::new();
        log.initialize().unwrap();
        log.activate().unwrap();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(log.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(), ServiceResult::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inactive_authority_prevents_service_invocation() {
        // The Log Authority is born Registered: its service must not be
        // reachable until the authority is Active.
        let log = LogAuthority::new();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            log.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_authority_invokes_its_proof_service() {
        // The Log Authority keeps the Phase 7F.1 proof service; its
        // invocation behavior is preserved.
        let mut log = LogAuthority::new();
        log.initialize().unwrap();
        log.activate().unwrap();
        let message = log_request();
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(log.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(), ServiceResult::Completed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_active_authority_forwards_real_domain_operations() {
        // Phase 7F.3: the authority forwards real domain operations to its
        // owned service, which carries domain state and answers questions
        // with the synchronous Response. The authority runs over an isolated
        // storage root (opening the workspace persists its state).
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-authority");
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        let open = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
        ));
        let open_invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&open);
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&open_invocation).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        let inspect = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
        ));
        let inspect_invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect);
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&inspect_invocation).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspend_transitions_active_to_suspended() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Suspended);
    }

    #[test]
    fn resume_transitions_suspended_to_active() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Active);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_transitions_active_to_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shutdown_transitions_suspended_to_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_full_lifecycle_chain_is_validated() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        // Registered → Initialized → Active → Suspended → Active → Shutdown.
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(workspace.lifecycle(), HubLifecycle::Shutdown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_lifecycle_transitions_are_rejected() {
        // Registered → Active: activation requires Initialized first.
        let mut registered = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(
            registered.activate(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        // Registered → Suspended: suspension requires Active.
        let mut registered = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        assert_eq!(
            registered.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Registered,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        // Initialized → Suspended: suspension requires Active.
        let mut initialized = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        initialized.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            initialized.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        // Initialized → Shutdown: shutdown requires Active or Suspended.
        let mut initialized = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        initialized.initialize().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            initialized.shutdown(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
                to: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
            })
        );
        // Shutdown is terminal: nothing leaves it.
        let mut shutdown = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        shutdown.initialize().unwrap();
        shutdown.activate().unwrap();
        shutdown.shutdown().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.initialize(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Initialized,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.activate(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.suspend(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Suspended,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.resume(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Active,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shutdown.shutdown(),
            Err(HubError::InvalidTransition {
                from: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
                to: HubLifecycle::Shutdown,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_unavailable_while_the_authority_is_suspended() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        // Suspension pauses the domain: services must not execute normal
        // operations while the owning authority is Suspended.
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn services_are_unavailable_after_shutdown() {
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::new();
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        workspace.shutdown().unwrap();
        let message = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        let invocation = ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        // Shutdown terminates the domain: services can never execute again.
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&invocation),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn suspension_preserves_the_domain_state_for_resume() {
        let dir = crate::test_support::TempDir::new("7h1-authority-suspend");
        let mut workspace = WorkspaceAuthority::with_storage_root(dir.path().to_owned());
        workspace.initialize().unwrap();
        workspace.activate().unwrap();
        // Open the workspace (real domain state, Phase 7F.3).
        let open = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Open("ra-main".to_owned()),
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&open)).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // Suspend and resume: the domain state must survive intact.
        workspace.suspend().unwrap();
        workspace.resume().unwrap();
        let inspect = crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessage::new(
            crate::hub::backbone::BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(crate::hub::BackbonePayload::Operation(
            crate::hub::ServiceOperation::Inspect,
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            workspace.invoke(&ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect)).unwrap(),
            ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }
}

=== BACKBONE ===
//! The Platform Backbone — the communication infrastructure of the RA
//! Software Platform (Phases 7E–7E.1).
//!
//! Architecturally this subsystem is the **Platform Backbone**; its
//! implementation is the **Message Backbone** (the earlier phase name is
//! preserved in prose throughout the codebase). The backbone is the single
//! communication path of the platform:
//!
//! `Frontend → PlatformInterface → Platform Backbone → Authority → Service →
//! RA Core Gateway (future) → RA Core`
//!
//! No layer may bypass the backbone. It transports **commands**, **requests**,
//! **responses**, **events**, **notifications**, **lifecycle signals** and
//! **platform broadcasts** between the platform hubs.
//!
//! * **Phase 7E** created the **communication contracts**: the message
//!   vocabulary, the message envelope and the backbone interface.
//! * **Phase 7E.1** turns those contracts into the **minimum real backbone
//!   runtime**: a deterministic, synchronous communication path
//!   (`accept → validate → resolve target → deliver → return result`). There
//!   is no asynchronous runtime, no queueing, no network transport, no
//!   persistence of messages and no message processing — delivery is the
//!   authority acknowledgment of receipt only (Phase 7F.1 lands the Service
//!   abstraction and the Log proof service behind the authorities).
//!
//! # Communication vocabulary
//!
//! [`BackboneMessageKind`] names the seven message kinds the backbone
//! transports; [`BackboneMessage`] is the envelope every kind travels in — a
//! kind, a source hub, an optional target hub (absent for platform-wide
//! messages such as broadcasts) and a domain-neutral [`BackbonePayload`].
//! Phase 7E.1 created the payload abstraction (empty); Phase 7F.2 adds the
//! minimal domain-neutral service operation payload
//! ([`BackbonePayload::Operation`]); Phase 7F.3 extends the vocabulary to the
//! real domain operations (`Open`, `Close`, `Set`, `Record`, `Clear`,
//! `Probe`). Phase 7F.4 completes the **Request → Response round-trip**: a
//! Request carries an opaque [`CorrelationId`]; the answering side converts
//! the service result into an explicit [`Response`] message that echoes the
//! correlation and is delivered back over the backbone to the requesting
//! caller. The correlation is the only way a Response identifies the Request
//! it answers. The backbone never processes payloads — it only transports
//! them.
//!
//! # Backbone interface
//!
//! [`Backbone`] is the backbone interface contract with the five
//! responsibilities of the phase: [`Backbone::accept`], [`Backbone::route`],
//! [`Backbone::dispatch`], [`Backbone::reply`] and [`Backbone::broadcast`].
//! Every method validates the envelope, the routing contract and the kind
//! contract of the operation — only platform-wide kinds (broadcast, platform
//! lifecycle signal) travel as broadcasts and only responses travel as
//! replies. **Phase 7E.1** makes the runtime real: `accept` validates,
//! `route` resolves the target, and `dispatch`/`reply`/`broadcast` deliver
//! through the target authority's delivery boundary and return a
//! [`DeliveryReceipt`]. There is still no queueing and no message
//! processing.
//!
//! # Kernel integration
//!
//! [`PlatformBackbone`] is the **first consumer** of the Platform Kernel's
//! communication contracts: the hub [`Registry`], the [`HubGraph`] topology,
//! the [`Router`] routing contracts and the [`BuiltinAuthorities`] authority
//! set. It is a short-lived borrowed view produced by
//! [`crate::hub::Kernel::backbone`]; the kernel owns the contracts and the
//! backbone consumes them. [`PlatformBackbone::is_attached`] verifies that
//! the backbone is wired onto a complete, consistent kernel and is part of
//! the kernel readiness check.
//!
//! # Authority ownership
//!
//! The platform ownership chain is fixed:
//!
//! `Authority → State → Services → Events → Policies`
//!
//! * an **authority owns exactly one domain** and owns the **state**, the
//!   **services**, the **events** and the **policies** of that domain;
//! * **services never own authorities** — an authority owns its services,
//!   never the other way around;
//! * the backbone dispatches to **authorities**; services are reached
//!   through their owning authority, never directly.
//!
//! # Scope
//!
//! Phase 7E: contracts. Phase 7E.1: the minimal real communication path —
//! deterministic synchronous delivery to Active authorities and delivery
//! receipts. Phase 7F.1: the common Service abstraction and the Log proof
//! service land behind the authorities. Phase 7F.2: the seven domain
//! services ride the backbone through their authorities, carrying the
//! minimal service-operation payload. Phase 7F.3: the payloads carry the
//! real domain operations, so the envelope owns its payload and is no longer
//! `Copy` — messages move through the backbone and are cloned when read
//! again. Phase 7F.4: the **Request → Response round-trip** — Requests
//! carry an opaque [`CorrelationId`], the service result is converted into
//! an explicit [`Response`] message through the
//! [`ResponsePayload::from_service_result`] boundary, and the Response is
//! delivered back over the backbone to the requesting caller; the envelope
//! gains the optional correlation field (the smallest compatible extension
//! the round-trip required). Phase 7F.5: the **backbone lifecycle gate** —
//! the backbone respects the platform lifecycle through its existing
//! per-authority `Active` gate (the one lifecycle gate; no second gate
//! exists): target resolution requires an `Active` authority, so while the
//! platform is suspended or shut down no authority is `Active`, dispatch and
//! reply reject normal traffic with [`HubError::InactiveTarget`] (no
//! fabricated deliveries for targeted operations), and a broadcast honestly
//! records zero recipients — no domain operation executes anywhere.
//! Suspension preserves domain state; shutdown terminates it.
//! Active objects, queueing, persistence of messages and business logic
//! remain later work. The future RA Core Gateway attaches behind the
//! backbone in a later phase.

use std::fmt;

use super::service::{ServiceOperation, ServiceResult};
use super::{
    BuiltinAuthorities, HubAuthority, HubDomain, HubError, HubGraph, HubId, HubLifecycle,
    HubResult, Registry, Router,
};

/// The kinds of messages the Platform Backbone transports.
///
/// The seven kinds are the platform's communication vocabulary: every
/// message travelling the backbone is exactly one of these.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(crate) enum BackboneMessageKind {
    /// A directive for an authority (or a service it owns) to perform an
    /// operation.
    Command,
    /// A question expecting a response.
    Request,
    /// The response to a request.
    Response,
    /// An unsolicited notification of a domain fact (state changed, ...).
    Event,
    /// An informational message; no response is expected.
    Notification,
    /// A message addressed to every hub of the platform.
    Broadcast,
    /// A platform or hub lifecycle signal (start, stop, suspend, ...).
    LifecycleSignal,
}

impl BackboneMessageKind {
    /// The seven message kinds of the backbone, in stable order.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests enumerate the vocabulary
    /// (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
