    pub(crate) const ALL: [BackboneMessageKind; 7] = [
        BackboneMessageKind::Command,
        BackboneMessageKind::Request,
        BackboneMessageKind::Response,
        BackboneMessageKind::Event,
        BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
        BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast,
        BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal,
    ];

    /// Returns the stable name of this message kind ("command", "request",
    /// ...).
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            BackboneMessageKind::Command => "command",
            BackboneMessageKind::Request => "request",
            BackboneMessageKind::Response => "response",
            BackboneMessageKind::Event => "event",
            BackboneMessageKind::Notification => "notification",
            BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast => "broadcast",
            BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal => "lifecycle-signal",
        }
    }

    /// Returns whether this kind may address the whole platform — i.e. may
    /// travel with no single target.
    ///
    /// Only broadcasts and platform-wide lifecycle signals are platform-wide
    /// in the Phase 7E vocabulary; every other kind always addresses a hub.
    pub(crate) fn is_platform_wide(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast | BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal
        )
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for BackboneMessageKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.name())
    }
}

/// A domain-neutral payload carried by a backbone message.
///
/// Phase 7E.1 introduces the minimum payload abstraction the seven message
/// kinds require; Phase 7F.2 adds the minimal domain-neutral service
/// operation; Phase 7F.3 extends the vocabulary to the real domain
/// operations, which own their arguments; Phase 7G.1 adds the storage
/// operations (`Save`, `Load`, `Recover`), whose `Save` carries the
/// **existing** `ra-persistence` `Artifact` representation (the one
/// documented exception to payload neutrality, mandated by the storage
/// phase: the platform reuses the existing artifact model and performs no
/// serialization of its own). It is deliberately **domain-neutral**: no
/// workspace, project, compiler or runtime payload types exist, and no
/// serialization happens in the backbone — the `Save` artifact is
/// serialized only by the storage stack (`Pss` → `Syss`).
///
/// The payload is **not `Copy`**: it owns its operation arguments (including
/// the storage `Save` artifact), so the message envelope ([`BackboneMessage`])
/// is not `Copy` either — messages move through the backbone, and a message
/// that must be read again after a move is cloned.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum BackbonePayload {
    /// No payload.
    None,
    /// A domain-neutral service operation (Phases 7F.2–7F.3).
    Operation(ServiceOperation),
    /// The explicit, strongly-typed payload of a Response message (Phase
    /// 7F.4).
    Response(ResponsePayload),
}

/// An envelope carried by the Platform Backbone.
///
/// A message is a [`BackboneMessageKind`], the hub it comes from (`source`),
/// the hub it is addressed to (`target`), an optional [`CorrelationId`]
/// (Phase 7F.4: set on the Request and Response messages of the round-trip,
/// so a Response identifies the Request it answers) and a domain-neutral
/// [`BackbonePayload`]. `target` is absent for platform-wide messages —
/// broadcasts and platform lifecycle signals.
///
/// The envelope is **not `Copy`**: it owns its payload, so a message moves
/// through the backbone (dispatch, reply, broadcast, accept, route all take
/// it by value) and is cloned when it must be read again after a move.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct BackboneMessage {
    kind: BackboneMessageKind,
    source: HubId,
    target: Option<HubId>,
    correlation: Option<CorrelationId>,
    payload: BackbonePayload,
}

impl BackboneMessage {
    /// Creates a message envelope carrying no payload.
    ///
    /// `target` is `None` for platform-wide messages (broadcasts, platform
    /// lifecycle signals) and `Some(hub)` for messages addressed to a single
    /// hub.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        kind: BackboneMessageKind,
        source: HubId,
        target: Option<HubId>,
    ) -> BackboneMessage {
        BackboneMessage {
            kind,
            source,
            target,
            correlation: None,
            payload: BackbonePayload::None,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the kind of this message.
    pub(crate) fn kind(&self) -> BackboneMessageKind {
        self.kind
    }

    /// Returns the hub this message comes from.
    pub(crate) fn source(&self) -> HubId {
        self.source
    }

    /// Returns the hub this message is addressed to, if any.
    ///
    /// `None` for platform-wide messages (broadcasts, platform lifecycle
    /// signals).
    pub(crate) fn target(&self) -> Option<HubId> {
        self.target
    }

    /// Returns the payload carried by this message.
    ///
    /// Read by the service invocation boundary
    /// ([`ServiceInvocation::operation`](crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::operation))
    /// since Phase 7F.2. The payload is cloned out of the envelope — the
    /// envelope itself stays owned by the caller.
    pub(crate) fn payload(&self) -> BackbonePayload {
        self.payload.clone()
    }

    /// Returns a copy of this message carrying `payload`.
    ///
    /// The only way to attach a payload to an envelope. Used since Phase
    /// 7F.2 to carry the minimal service operation.
    pub(crate) fn with_payload(mut self, payload: BackbonePayload) -> BackboneMessage {
        self.payload = payload;
        self
    }

    /// Returns the correlation identifier of this message, if any.
    ///
    /// `None` on messages that carry no correlation (every Phase 7E–7F.3
    /// envelope); `Some` on the Request and Response messages of the Phase
    /// 7F.4 round-trip.
    pub(crate) fn correlation(&self) -> Option<CorrelationId> {
        self.correlation
    }

    /// Returns a copy of this message carrying `correlation`.
    ///
    /// The only way to attach a correlation identifier to an envelope. Used
    /// since Phase 7F.4 by the Request → Response round-trip, so a Response
    /// identifies the Request it answers.
    pub(crate) fn with_correlation(mut self, correlation: CorrelationId) -> BackboneMessage {
        self.correlation = Some(correlation);
        self
    }
}

/// The status of a message that moved through the backbone runtime.
///
/// The result contract of Phase 7E.1: a message is either **accepted** (the
/// envelope and routing contract hold), **delivered** (the target authority
/// acknowledged receipt) or **rejected**. Rejection is expressed through the
/// existing SySS/Hub error vocabulary — a rejected message returns
/// [`Err(HubError)`](HubError) instead of a receipt — so the receipt itself
/// only carries the two successful states.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum BackboneStatus {
    /// The message passed validation and (for routing) target resolution;
    /// nothing was delivered.
    Accepted,
    /// The message was delivered to its target authority (or to every Active
    /// authority, for platform-wide messages).
    Delivered,
}

/// A delivery receipt returned by the backbone runtime.
///
/// The minimal result contract of Phase 7E.1: it records what happened to a
/// message as it moved through the backbone — the kind, the source and
/// target hubs, the final [`BackboneStatus`] and, for deliveries, how many
/// authorities acknowledged it. It carries enough information for future
/// Response handling (a Response can be addressed back to the receipt's
/// source hub).
///
/// Rejection is **not** a receipt: a rejected message returns
/// [`Err(HubError)`](HubError) from the backbone operation instead.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct DeliveryReceipt {
    kind: BackboneMessageKind,
    source: HubId,
    target: Option<HubId>,
    status: BackboneStatus,
    recipients: usize,
}

impl DeliveryReceipt {
    /// A receipt for a message that passed validation and routing but was
    /// not delivered.
    pub(crate) fn accepted(message: &BackboneMessage) -> DeliveryReceipt {
        DeliveryReceipt {
            kind: message.kind(),
            source: message.source(),
            target: message.target(),
            status: BackboneStatus::Accepted,
            recipients: 0,
        }
    }

    /// A receipt for a message that `recipients` authorities acknowledged.
    pub(crate) fn delivered(message: &BackboneMessage, recipients: usize) -> DeliveryReceipt {
        DeliveryReceipt {
            kind: message.kind(),
            source: message.source(),
            target: message.target(),
            status: BackboneStatus::Delivered,
            recipients,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the kind of the message this receipt describes.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect receipts
    /// (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn kind(&self) -> BackboneMessageKind {
        self.kind
    }

    /// Returns the source hub of the message this receipt describes.
    ///
    /// The hub a future Response to this message would be addressed to.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect receipts
    /// (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn source(&self) -> HubId {
        self.source
    }

    /// Returns the target hub of the message this receipt describes, if any.
    ///
    /// `None` for platform-wide messages.
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect receipts
    /// (TODO(Phase7F)).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn target(&self) -> Option<HubId> {
        self.target
    }

    /// Returns the final status of the message this receipt describes.
    pub(crate) fn status(&self) -> BackboneStatus {
        self.status
    }

    /// Returns how many authorities acknowledged the message.
    ///
    /// `0` for accepted (non-delivered) receipts; `1` for a targeted
    /// delivery; the number of Active authorities for a platform-wide
    /// delivery (the aggregate receipt of [`Backbone::broadcast`]).
    pub(crate) fn recipients(&self) -> usize {
        self.recipients
    }
}

/// The opaque correlation identifier of a Request → Response exchange
/// (Phase 7F.4).
///
/// A Response identifies the Request it answers through its correlation
/// identifier. Identifiers are **opaque** — only a [`CorrelationSequence`]
/// can mint them — and deterministic: sequential and testable, never derived
/// from timestamps, memory addresses or randomness.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(crate) struct CorrelationId(u64);

impl fmt::Display for CorrelationId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.0)
    }
}

/// A deterministic correlation mint: yields sequential [`CorrelationId`]s.
///
/// Owned by the requesting endpoint — the platform in the Phase 7F.4 proof
/// path ([`crate::SySS::request`]) — and by tests. Each call to
/// [`next`](CorrelationSequence::next) yields the next identifier in the
/// sequence (1, 2, 3, ...). No global mutable state, no timestamps, no
/// addresses, no randomness.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(crate) struct CorrelationSequence(u64);

impl CorrelationSequence {
    /// Creates a fresh correlation sequence.
    pub(crate) fn new() -> CorrelationSequence {
        CorrelationSequence(0)
    }

    /// Yields the next correlation identifier in the sequence.
    pub(crate) fn next(&mut self) -> CorrelationId {
        self.0 += 1;
        CorrelationId(self.0)
    }
}

/// The explicit, strongly-typed payload of a Response message (Phase 7F.4).
///
/// Carried by [`BackbonePayload::Response`]. It is the **communication**
/// outcome of a Request → Response exchange — deliberately distinct from
/// [`ServiceResult`](crate::hub::ServiceResult) (the service execution
/// outcome) and [`DeliveryReceipt`] (the transport/delivery outcome); the
/// mapping from a service result is explicit
/// ([`ResponsePayload::from_service_result`]) and never collapses the
/// outcomes.
///
/// Richer, domain-specific response payloads are future work; this is the
/// smallest strongly-typed representation the round-trip requires. Phase
/// 7G.1 adds the storage answers ([`ResponsePayload::Loaded`],
/// [`ResponsePayload::Recovered`]) for the real storage operations. No
/// serialization, no `HashMap<String, Any>`, no untyped blobs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ResponsePayload {
    /// The request was accepted (informational).
    Accepted,
    /// The requested operation completed.
    Completed,
    /// The request was rejected.
    Rejected,
    /// The request was answered with an inspected state summary.
    Inspected(String),
    /// A storage `Load` was answered with the loaded artifact representation
    /// (Phase 7G.1).
    Loaded(String),
    /// A storage `Recover` was answered with the recovery report summary
    /// (Phase 7G.1).
    Recovered(String),
    /// A document `OpenDocument` was answered with the opened document
    /// summary (Phase 7H).
    Opened(String),
}

impl ResponsePayload {
    /// The explicit conversion boundary: a [`ServiceResult`] (the service
    /// execution outcome) → the response payload (the communication outcome).
    ///
    /// Every [`ServiceResult`] variant maps to exactly one response payload
    /// variant; the mapping is total and one-to-one, so a transport receipt
    /// is never mistaken for a successful service execution.
    pub(crate) fn from_service_result(result: ServiceResult) -> ResponsePayload {
        match result {
            ServiceResult::Accepted => ResponsePayload::Accepted,
            ServiceResult::Completed => ResponsePayload::Completed,
            ServiceResult::Rejected => ResponsePayload::Rejected,
            ServiceResult::Inspected(summary) => ResponsePayload::Inspected(summary),
            ServiceResult::Loaded(summary) => ResponsePayload::Loaded(summary),
            ServiceResult::Recovered(summary) => ResponsePayload::Recovered(summary),
            ServiceResult::Opened(summary) => ResponsePayload::Opened(summary),
        }
    }
}

/// The explicit Response contract of the Request → Response round-trip
/// (Phase 7F.4).
///
/// The message returned to the requesting caller. Distinct from:
///
/// * [`DeliveryReceipt`] — the **transport/delivery** outcome;
/// * [`ServiceResult`](crate::hub::ServiceResult) — the **service
///   execution** outcome;
/// * a Request — a Response answers one specific correlated Request.
///
/// A Response is a [`BackboneMessage`] of kind
/// [`BackboneMessageKind::Response`] addressed back to the requesting
/// endpoint, echoing the Request's [`CorrelationId`] and carrying an
/// explicit [`ResponsePayload`]. It is delivered over the backbone with
/// [`Backbone::reply`] — the existing routing and validation, never a
/// second response router.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Response {
    message: BackboneMessage,
    payload: ResponsePayload,
}

impl Response {
    /// Creates a Response addressed to `target` (the requesting caller) from
    /// `source` (the answering authority), echoing the Request's
    /// `correlation` and carrying `payload`.
    ///
    /// `correlation` is `None` only to prove that a missing correlation is
    /// rejected at the verification boundary; the round-trip always supplies
    /// one.
    ///
    /// The payload is stored once on the Response and also embedded in the
    /// Response message, so the delivered envelope **is** the response (the
    /// two are written together at construction and never diverge).
    pub(crate) fn new(
        source: HubId,
        target: HubId,
        correlation: Option<CorrelationId>,
        payload: ResponsePayload,
    ) -> Response {
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Response, source, Some(target));
        let message = match correlation {
            Some(correlation) => message.with_correlation(correlation),
            None => message,
        };
        let message = message.with_payload(BackbonePayload::Response(payload.clone()));
        Response { message, payload }
    }

    /// Returns the underlying Response message.
    pub(crate) fn message(&self) -> &BackboneMessage {
        &self.message
    }

    /// Returns the kind of this Response's message — always
    /// [`BackboneMessageKind::Response`].
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect Responses
    /// (Phase 7F.4).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn kind(&self) -> BackboneMessageKind {
        self.message.kind()
    }

    /// Returns the answering authority (the source of the Response message).
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect Responses
    /// (Phase 7F.4).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn source(&self) -> HubId {
        self.message.source()
    }

    /// Returns the requesting caller (the target of the Response message).
    ///
    /// Not yet consumed by the lib build: the tests inspect Responses
    /// (Phase 7F.4).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn target(&self) -> Option<HubId> {
        self.message.target()
    }

    /// Returns the correlation identifier echoed from the Request this
    /// Response answers, if any.
    pub(crate) fn correlation(&self) -> Option<CorrelationId> {
        self.message.correlation()
    }

    /// Returns the explicit response payload.
    pub(crate) fn payload(&self) -> &ResponsePayload {
        &self.payload
    }

    /// Returns whether this Response answers the Request that carried
    /// `expected`: the correlation identifiers match.
    pub(crate) fn answers(&self, expected: CorrelationId) -> bool {
        self.correlation() == Some(expected)
    }

    /// Verifies this Response answers the Request that carried `expected`.
    ///
    /// The correlation-safety boundary of the round-trip: a Response whose
    /// correlation does not match — or that carries no correlation at all —
    /// is rejected with [`HubError::CorrelationMismatch`]. Used by the
    /// round-trip orchestrator ([`crate::SySS::request`]) as a defensive,
    /// deterministic check.
    pub(crate) fn verify_answers(&self, expected: CorrelationId) -> HubResult<()> {
        if self.answers(expected) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
                expected,
                actual: self.correlation(),
            })
        }
    }
}

/// The Backbone interface — the communication contract of the platform.
///
/// Phase 7E defined the contract; **Phase 7E.1** implements the minimal real
/// runtime behind it. Every operation validates the envelope, the routing
/// contract and the kind contract, returns a [`DeliveryReceipt`] on success
/// and rejects with a [`HubError`] otherwise. There is no queueing and no
/// message processing (TODO(Phase7F)).
pub(crate) trait Backbone {
    /// Accepts an inbound message at the backbone boundary.
    ///
    /// Contract: `source` must be a registered hub; a targeted message must
    /// not target its own source and must target a registered hub.
    ///
    /// Returns an **accepted** receipt; nothing is resolved or delivered.
    fn accept(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt>;

    /// Routes `message` toward its target hub.
    ///
    /// Contract: the message must be targeted (broadcasts are routed with
    /// [`Backbone::broadcast`]); a route from source to target must exist (no
    /// self-routes) and both endpoints must be registered. The target is
    /// **resolved** — it exists, is registered, has an authority and is
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`].
    ///
    /// Returns an **accepted** receipt; no delivery is performed.
    fn route(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt>;

    /// Dispatches `message` to the target authority.
    ///
    /// Contract: the message must be targeted; the target must be a
    /// registered authority in the [`HubLifecycle::Active`] state (only
    /// active hubs are routed to). The message is **delivered** through the
    /// target authority's delivery boundary.
    ///
    /// Returns a **delivered** receipt.
    fn dispatch(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt>;

    /// Sends `reply` back over the backbone to the request's source.
    ///
    /// Contract: `reply` must be a [`BackboneMessageKind::Response`] — a
    /// reply is the response to a request — addressed to a concrete hub (the
    /// request's source), and its envelope must be valid (registered source,
    /// no self-target). The reply is **delivered** to the target authority.
    ///
    /// Returns a **delivered** receipt.
    fn reply(&mut self, reply: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt>;

    /// Broadcasts `message` to every hub of the platform.
    ///
    /// Contract: a broadcast addresses the whole platform — it carries no
    /// single target and its kind must be platform-wide
    /// ([`BackboneMessageKind::is_platform_wide`]: broadcast or lifecycle
    /// signal). The message is **delivered** to every
    /// [`HubLifecycle::Active`] authority; inactive authorities never receive
    /// platform messages.
    ///
    /// Returns a **delivered** receipt recording how many authorities
    /// acknowledged it.
    fn broadcast(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt>;
}

/// The Platform Backbone — the concrete backbone surface.
///
/// A short-lived borrowed view over the Platform Kernel's communication
/// contracts: the hub [`Registry`], the [`HubGraph`] topology, the [`Router`]
/// routing contracts and the [`BuiltinAuthorities`] authority set. The kernel
/// owns those contracts; [`crate::hub::Kernel::backbone`] produces the view
/// and the kernel readiness check verifies it is attached.
///
/// This is the **first consumer** of the registry, the graph, the routing
/// contracts and the authorities. It owns no domain logic and implements the
/// [`Backbone`] interface as the Phase 7E.1 runtime: envelope validation,
/// target resolution (exists, registered, authority present, Active) and
/// delivery through the authority delivery boundary.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct PlatformBackbone<'a> {
    registry: &'a Registry,
    graph: &'a HubGraph,
    router: &'a Router,
    authorities: &'a BuiltinAuthorities,
}

impl<'a> PlatformBackbone<'a> {
    /// Attaches the backbone onto the kernel's communication contracts.
    pub(crate) fn attach(
        registry: &'a Registry,
        graph: &'a HubGraph,
        router: &'a Router,
        authorities: &'a BuiltinAuthorities,
    ) -> PlatformBackbone<'a> {
        PlatformBackbone {
            registry,
            graph,
            router,
            authorities,
        }
    }

    /// Returns whether the backbone is attached onto a complete, consistent
    /// kernel:
    ///
    /// * the registry records every built-in authority;
    /// * the graph knows every authority and resolves each one to its own
    ///   domain, its domain knowledge is complete and its relationship
    ///   knowledge is complete;
    /// * the router can route between every pair of distinct hubs.
    ///
    /// Structural verification only — no message processing. It is part of
    /// the kernel readiness check ([`crate::hub::Kernel::is_ready`]).
    pub(crate) fn is_attached(&self) -> bool {
        let registry_complete = self.registry.len() == HubId::ALL.len()
            && self
                .authorities
                .iter()
                .all(|authority| self.registry.contains(authority.id()));
        // The graph's domain knowledge is complete (every initial domain
        // resolves to its owner) and consistent with the authority set (every
        // authority is known to the graph and resolves to itself).
        let graph_complete = self.graph.len() == HubId::ALL.len()
            && HubDomain::ALL.iter().all(|domain| {
                self.graph.authority_for(*domain) == Some(HubId::from_domain(*domain))
            })
            && self.authorities.iter().all(|authority| {
                self.graph.contains(authority.id())
                    && self.graph.authority_for(authority.domain()) == Some(authority.id())
            })
            && self.graph.relationships().len() == HubId::ALL.len();
        let routing_complete = self.authorities.iter().all(|source| {
            self.authorities.iter().all(|target| {
                source.id() == target.id() || self.router.route(source.id(), target.id()).is_ok()
            })
        });
        registry_complete && graph_complete && routing_complete
    }

    /// Returns whether the backbone is **operational**: the Phase 7E.1
    /// runtime succeeds on the authority set.
    ///
    /// A targeted command between two authorities is accepted, routed and
    /// **delivered** (a delivered receipt); a reply flows back and is
    /// delivered; and a platform broadcast is delivered to every Active
    /// authority. The probe hubs are derived from the authority set itself,
    /// so the check adapts to whatever authorities the kernel runs on. This
    /// is a verification smoke test of the communication runtime — part of
    /// kernel readiness ([`crate::hub::Kernel::is_ready`]) — not message
    /// processing and not business logic.
    pub(crate) fn is_operational(&mut self) -> bool {
        // The probe source, target and broadcaster are taken from the
        // authority set, never hard-coded; fewer than three authorities
        // cannot be operational.
        let mut authorities = self.authorities.iter();
        let Some(source) = authorities.next() else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(target) = authorities.next() else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(broadcaster) = authorities.next() else {
            return false;
        };

        let probe =
            BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Command, source.id(), Some(target.id()));
        // `probe` is read again below (`accept`), so it is cloned into
        // dispatch: the envelope owns its payload and is not `Copy`.
        let dispatched = matches!(
            self.dispatch(probe.clone()),
            Ok(receipt) if receipt.status() == BackboneStatus::Delivered
        );
        let replied = matches!(
            self.reply(BackboneMessage::new(
                BackboneMessageKind::Response,
                target.id(),
                Some(source.id()),
            )),
            Ok(receipt) if receipt.status() == BackboneStatus::Delivered
        );
        let broadcast = matches!(
            self.broadcast(BackboneMessage::new(
                BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast,
                broadcaster.id(),
                None,
            )),
            Ok(receipt)
                if receipt.status() == BackboneStatus::Delivered && receipt.recipients() > 0
        );
        // `probe` is consumed by both `accept` and `route`; the envelope is
        // not `Copy`, so the first use clones it.
        self.accept(probe.clone()).is_ok()
            && self.route(probe).is_ok()
            && dispatched
            && replied
            && broadcast
    }

    /// Validates the envelope of `message` against the registry.
    ///
    /// The source must be a registered hub; a targeted message must not
    /// target its own source and must target a registered hub.
    fn validate_envelope(&self, message: &BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<()> {
        if self.registry.lookup(message.source()).is_none() {
            return Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(message.source()));
        }
        if let Some(target) = message.target() {
            if target == message.source() {
                return Err(HubError::SelfRoute(target));
            }
            if self.registry.lookup(target).is_none() {
                return Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(target));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Resolves the target of `message` for routing and delivery.
    ///
    /// Verifies, in order:
    ///
    /// 1. the message is **targeted** ([`HubError::TargetRequired`]);
    /// 2. the target **exists** — it is known to the hub [`Registry`] and
    ///    the [`HubGraph`] topology ([`HubError::UnregisteredTarget`]);
    /// 3. a **target authority** exists for the target
    ///    ([`HubError::UnregisteredTarget`]);
    /// 4. the target authority is **Active** ([`HubError::InactiveTarget`]).
    ///
    /// Resolution uses the existing contracts only — the registry, the graph
    /// and the authority set — never a second registry or a second routing
    /// system.
    fn resolve_target(&self, message: &BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<&dyn HubAuthority> {
        let target = message.target().ok_or(HubError::TargetRequired)?;
        // 1 & 2. The target exists: it is registered and known to the graph.
        if self.registry.lookup(target).is_none() || !self.graph.contains(target) {
            return Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(target));
        }
        // 3. The target authority exists.
        let authority = self
            .authorities
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == target)
            .ok_or(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(target))?;
        // 4. The target authority is Active: inactive authorities must not
        //    receive normal platform messages.
        if authority.lifecycle() != HubLifecycle::Active {
            return Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(target));
        }
        Ok(authority)
    }
}

impl Backbone for PlatformBackbone<'_> {
    fn accept(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt> {
        self.validate_envelope(&message)?;
        Ok(DeliveryReceipt::accepted(&message))
    }

    fn route(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt> {
        self.validate_envelope(&message)?;
        let authority = self.resolve_target(&message)?;
        // The routing contract: a route from source to target must exist (no
        // self-routes).
        self.router.route(message.source(), authority.id())?;
        Ok(DeliveryReceipt::accepted(&message))
    }

    fn dispatch(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt> {
        self.validate_envelope(&message)?;
        let authority = self.resolve_target(&message)?;
        self.router.route(message.source(), authority.id())?;
        // Deliver through the authority's controlled delivery boundary; the
        // authority's acknowledgment **is** the delivery receipt.
        Ok(authority.receive(&message))
    }

    fn reply(&mut self, reply: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt> {
        self.validate_envelope(&reply)?;
        // A reply is the response to a request: only Response messages travel
        // back over the backbone as replies.
        if reply.kind() != BackboneMessageKind::Response {
            return Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: reply.kind(),
                operation: "sent as a reply",
            });
        }
        // A response addresses the request's source hub — it always carries a
        // concrete target; the resolved authority acknowledges it and its
        // acknowledgment **is** the delivery receipt.
        let authority = self.resolve_target(&reply)?;
        Ok(authority.receive(&reply))
    }

    fn broadcast(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> HubResult<DeliveryReceipt> {
        // A broadcast addresses the whole platform — it carries no single
        // target.
        if message.target().is_some() {
            return Err(HubError::TargetedBroadcast);
        }
        // Only platform-wide kinds may travel as broadcasts; a targeted kind
        // (command, request, ...) always addresses a hub.
        if !message.kind().is_platform_wide() {
            return Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: message.kind(),
                operation: "broadcast",
            });
        }
        self.validate_envelope(&message)?;
        // Deliver to every Active authority; inactive authorities never
        // receive platform messages.
        let mut recipients = 0;
        for authority in self.authorities.iter() {
            if authority.lifecycle() == HubLifecycle::Active {
                authority.receive(&message);
                recipients += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(DeliveryReceipt::delivered(&message, recipients))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::hub::{Hub, Kernel, KernelInitializer};

    /// A kernel brought online by the initializer (all authorities Active).
    fn ready_kernel() -> Kernel {
        KernelInitializer::new().initialize().unwrap()
    }

    /// The owned pieces of a deliberately incomplete attachment: only the
    /// workspace and storage hubs are registered, and the authorities are
    /// still [`HubLifecycle::Registered`].
    fn partial_attachment() -> (Registry, HubGraph, Router, BuiltinAuthorities) {
        let mut registry = Registry::new();
        registry.register(Hub::new(HubDomain::Workspace)).unwrap();
        registry.register(Hub::new(HubDomain::Storage)).unwrap();
        let mut graph = HubGraph::new();
        graph.register(Hub::new(HubDomain::Workspace)).unwrap();
        graph.register(Hub::new(HubDomain::Storage)).unwrap();
        (registry, graph, Router::new(), BuiltinAuthorities::new())
    }

    #[test]
    fn vocabulary_has_the_seven_message_kinds() {
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::ALL.len(), 7);
        for (i, a) in BackboneMessageKind::ALL.iter().enumerate() {
            for (j, b) in BackboneMessageKind::ALL.iter().enumerate() {
                if i != j {
                    assert_ne!(a, b, "message kinds {a} and {b} collide");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_kinds_print_stably() {
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::Command.to_string(), "command");
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::Request.to_string(), "request");
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::Response.to_string(), "response");
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::Event.to_string(), "event");
        assert_eq!(
            BackboneMessageKind::Notification.to_string(),
            "notification"
        );
        assert_eq!(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast.to_string(), "broadcast");
        assert_eq!(
            BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal.to_string(),
            "lifecycle-signal"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn envelope_records_kind_source_and_target() {
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        assert_eq!(message.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Request);
        assert_eq!(message.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(message.target(), Some(HubId::STORAGE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn platform_wide_messages_carry_no_target() {
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(message.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast);
        assert_eq!(message.source(), HubId::LOG);
        assert_eq!(message.target(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_attaches_to_a_ready_kernel() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        assert!(kernel.backbone().is_attached());
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_detects_an_incomplete_kernel() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        assert!(!backbone.is_attached());
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_is_operational_on_a_ready_kernel() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        assert!(backbone.is_operational());
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_is_not_operational_when_incomplete() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        assert!(!backbone.is_operational());
    }

    #[test]
    fn accept_accepts_a_valid_envelope() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        assert!(backbone.accept(message).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn accept_rejects_an_unregistered_source() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::LOG,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.accept(message),
            Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accept_rejects_a_self_target() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::DEVICE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.accept(message),
            Err(HubError::SelfRoute(HubId::DEVICE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn route_routes_between_registered_hubs() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::SETTINGS,
            Some(HubId::HISTORY),
        );
        assert!(backbone.route(message).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn route_rejects_a_platform_wide_message() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(backbone.route(message), Err(HubError::TargetRequired));
    }

    #[test]
    fn route_rejects_an_unregistered_target() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.route(message),
            Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn route_rejects_a_self_route() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::PROJECT,
            Some(HubId::PROJECT),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.route(message),
            Err(HubError::SelfRoute(HubId::PROJECT))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_dispatches_to_an_active_authority() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        assert!(backbone.dispatch(message).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_inactive_authority() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        // Storage is registered but its authority is still Registered: only
        // Active hubs are dispatched to.
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_unregistered_authority() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_accepts_a_valid_reply() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let reply = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Response,
            HubId::STORAGE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert!(backbone.reply(reply).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_accepts_a_platform_wide_message() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert!(backbone.broadcast(message).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_rejects_a_single_target() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast,
            HubId::LOG,
            Some(HubId::DEVICE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::TargetedBroadcast)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_accepts_a_platform_lifecycle_signal() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert!(backbone.broadcast(message).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_rejects_a_targeted_kind() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A command always addresses a hub; it cannot travel as a broadcast.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Command, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                operation: "broadcast",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_requires_a_response_kind() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::STORAGE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.reply(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Command,
                operation: "sent as a reply",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_requires_a_concrete_target() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A response addresses the request's source hub: it carries a target.
        let reply = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Response, HubId::STORAGE, None);
        assert_eq!(backbone.reply(reply), Err(HubError::TargetRequired));
    }

    #[test]
    fn platform_wide_kinds_are_broadcast_and_lifecycle_signals() {
        assert!(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast.is_platform_wide());
        assert!(BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal.is_platform_wide());
        for kind in [
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            BackboneMessageKind::Response,
            BackboneMessageKind::Event,
            BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
        ] {
            assert!(!kind.is_platform_wide(), "{kind} must always be targeted");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn accept_returns_an_accepted_receipt() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.accept(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Accepted);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 0);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Request);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::STORAGE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn route_resolves_the_target_and_returns_an_accepted_receipt() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::SETTINGS,
            Some(HubId::HISTORY),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.route(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Accepted);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::SETTINGS);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::HISTORY));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_delivers_a_request() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Request);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::STORAGE));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_delivers_a_command() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::PROJECT,
            Some(HubId::PACKAGE),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Command);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_delivers_a_response_back() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let reply = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Response,
            HubId::STORAGE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.reply(reply).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::STORAGE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_delivers_to_every_active_authority() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::LOG, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), None);
        assert_eq!(
            receipt.recipients(),
            HubId::ALL.len(),
            "every Active authority must acknowledge the broadcast"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_delivers_a_platform_lifecycle_signal() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal, HubId::LOG, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::LifecycleSignal);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), None);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), HubId::ALL.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_skips_inactive_authorities() {
        // The authorities are born Registered and never activated: nothing is
        // Active, so a broadcast delivers to nobody — inactive authorities
        // never receive platform messages.
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::WORKSPACE, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn messages_carry_a_domain_neutral_payload() {
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Notification,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::None);
        assert_eq!(message.payload(), BackbonePayload::None);
        // The plain constructor also carries the empty payload.
        let plain = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Notification, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(plain.payload(), BackbonePayload::None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_a_log_request_to_the_log_service() {
        // Phase 7F.1 proof chain: Backbone → LogAuthority → LogService →
        // ServiceResult.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        // 1. The backbone delivers the proof request to the Log Authority
        //    (cloned: the message is read again below for the invocation).
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::LOG));
        // 2. The Log Authority forwards it to its owned service, which
        //    returns its ServiceResult.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::LOG)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the log authority");
        let invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_a_domain_request_to_its_service() {
        // Phase 7F.2 chain: Backbone → WorkspaceAuthority → WorkspaceService
        // → ServiceResult, carrying the minimal service-operation payload.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Accept));
        // 1. The backbone delivers the request to the Workspace Authority
        //    (cloned: the message is read again below for the invocation).
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(message.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        // 2. The Workspace Authority forwards it to its owned service.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::WORKSPACE)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the workspace authority");
        let invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&message);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn backbone_delivers_real_operations_to_the_workspace_domain() {
        // Phase 7F.3 chain: Backbone → WorkspaceAuthority → WorkspaceService
        // → domain state → ServiceResult / Response, carrying the real
        // domain operation payload.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let open = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Open(
            "ra-main".to_owned(),
        )));
        // 1. The backbone delivers the open operation to the Workspace
        //    Authority (cloned: the message is read again below).
        let receipt = backbone.dispatch(open.clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::WORKSPACE));
        // 2. The Workspace Authority forwards it to its owned service, which
        //    performs the real domain operation.
        let authority = kernel
            .authorities()
            .iter()
            .find(|authority| authority.id() == HubId::WORKSPACE)
            .expect("the ready kernel owns the workspace authority");
        let open_invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&open);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&open_invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Completed
        );
        // 3. A question is answered with the real domain state — the
        //    synchronous Response path.
        let inspect = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Inspect));
        let inspect_invocation = crate::hub::service::ServiceInvocation::new(&inspect);
        assert_eq!(
            authority.invoke(&inspect_invocation).unwrap(),
            crate::hub::service::ServiceResult::Inspected("workspace: ra-main".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn correlation_sequences_are_sequential_and_deterministic() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let first = sequence.next();
        let second = sequence.next();
        assert_ne!(first, second, "correlation ids must be distinct");
        assert_eq!(first.to_string(), "1");
        assert_eq!(second.to_string(), "2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn messages_carry_an_optional_correlation_identifier() {
        // Every Phase 7E–7F.3 envelope carries no correlation; the round-trip
        // attaches one through `with_correlation`.
        let plain = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(plain.correlation(), None);
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let request = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        )
        .with_correlation(correlation)
        .with_payload(BackbonePayload::Operation(ServiceOperation::Inspect));
        assert_eq!(request.correlation(), Some(correlation));
    }

    #[test]
    fn service_results_map_explicitly_to_response_payloads() {
        // The explicit ServiceResult → Response conversion boundary: every
        // service outcome maps to exactly one response payload.
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Accepted),
            ResponsePayload::Accepted
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Completed),
            ResponsePayload::Completed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Rejected),
            ResponsePayload::Rejected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ResponsePayload::from_service_result(ServiceResult::Inspected("x".to_owned())),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("x".to_owned())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_is_a_correlated_response_message() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(correlation),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()),
        );
        assert_eq!(response.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(response.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(response.target(), Some(HubId::DEVICE));
        assert_eq!(response.correlation(), Some(correlation));
        assert_eq!(
            response.payload(),
            &ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned())
        );
        // The Response message itself carries the response payload.
        assert_eq!(
            response.message().payload(),
            BackbonePayload::Response(ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_answers_the_request_it_correlates_with() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let request = sequence.next();
        let other = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(request),
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert!(response.answers(request));
        assert!(
            !response.answers(other),
            "a response never answers an unrelated request"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn verify_answers_rejects_a_mismatched_or_missing_correlation() {
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let request = sequence.next();
        let other = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(request),
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert!(response.verify_answers(request).is_ok());
        // A mismatched correlation is rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            response.verify_answers(other),
            Err(HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
                expected: other,
                actual: Some(request),
            })
        );
        // A missing correlation identifier is rejected.
        let missing = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            None,
            ResponsePayload::Completed,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            missing.verify_answers(request),
            Err(HubError::CorrelationMismatch {
                expected: request,
                actual: None,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_request_cannot_be_broadcast() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A request always addresses a hub; it cannot travel as a broadcast.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Request,
                operation: "broadcast",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_response_cannot_be_broadcast() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A response always addresses the requesting caller; it cannot travel
        // as a broadcast.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Response, HubId::LOG, None);
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.broadcast(message),
            Err(HubError::InvalidMessageKind {
                kind: BackboneMessageKind::Response,
                operation: "broadcast",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_requires_a_concrete_target_for_requests() {
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        // A request always addresses a hub: a target-less request is
        // rejected.
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Request, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        assert_eq!(backbone.dispatch(message), Err(HubError::TargetRequired));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_unregistered_request_target() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::UnregisteredTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_an_inactive_request_target() {
        let (registry, graph, router, authorities) = partial_attachment();
        let mut backbone = PlatformBackbone::attach(&registry, &graph, &router, &authorities);
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            Some(HubId::STORAGE),
        );
        // Storage is registered but its authority is still Registered: only
        // Active hubs are dispatched to.
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::STORAGE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reply_delivers_a_correlated_response_back_to_the_caller() {
        // Phase 7F.4: a Response echoing the Request's correlation is
        // delivered back over the backbone to the requesting caller.
        let kernel = ready_kernel();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let mut sequence = CorrelationSequence::new();
        let correlation = sequence.next();
        let response = Response::new(
            HubId::WORKSPACE,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(correlation),
            ResponsePayload::Inspected("workspace: none".to_owned()),
        );
        let receipt = backbone.reply(response.message().clone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.kind(), BackboneMessageKind::Response);
        assert_eq!(receipt.source(), HubId::WORKSPACE);
        assert_eq!(receipt.target(), Some(HubId::DEVICE));
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_normal_traffic_while_the_platform_is_suspended() {
        // Phase 7F.5: suspension moves every authority out of Active; the
        // backbone lifecycle gate (the existing per-authority Active gate)
        // then rejects normal service requests instead of fabricating a
        // successful delivery receipt.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Request,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::WORKSPACE),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::WORKSPACE))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_rejects_normal_traffic_after_shutdown() {
        // Phase 7F.5: shutdown terminates every authority; normal requests
        // are rejected permanently — no new traffic enters the platform.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.shutdown().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(
            BackboneMessageKind::Command,
            HubId::DEVICE,
            Some(HubId::LOG),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            backbone.dispatch(message),
            Err(HubError::InactiveTarget(HubId::LOG))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn broadcast_reaches_no_authority_while_suspended() {
        // Phase 7F.5: a platform-wide broadcast is delivered to every Active
        // authority — while the platform is suspended none is Active, so the
        // receipt records zero recipients and no domain operation executes.
        let mut kernel = ready_kernel();
        kernel.suspend().unwrap();
        let mut backbone = kernel.backbone();
        let message = BackboneMessage::new(BackboneMessageKind::Broadcast, HubId::DEVICE, None);
        let receipt = backbone.broadcast(message).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(receipt.status(), BackboneStatus::Delivered);
        assert_eq!(receipt.recipients(), 0);
    }
}
